articles.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer
articles.summary:
Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators

Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a…

blocks.text: Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic Gromit to show surprise.

Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of the Aardman studio seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets that starred in Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.
Sought-after items included Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models from the studio’s hugely popular 2024 film Vengeance Most Fowl.

Lot 216, for example, was Wallace in his traditional outfit of a knitted green tank top, red tie and brown trousers. The catalogue said he was in “smashing condition”, and gave details of his construction: “Wallace’s head is moulded from clay; while his body is made of silicone to facilitate smooth repositioning by the animators.
“He has a skeleton, just like every salt-of-the-earth lad, it’s just that his happens to be made of metal. His teeth, shirt collar, tie, pen, and pencil are fast-cast resin and his eyes are plastic.”
A puppet of Gromit on all fours from the same film – lot 219 – was “crafted over a fully jointed internal metal armature, allowing him to be held in his most natural pose”.

The catalogue made it clear these were not toys but pieces of art needing special packaging, shipping and careful handling. “Please also be aware that exposure to extreme temperatures may cause damage,” it said.

blocks.caption: Feathers McGraw alongside CI Mackintosh. Photograph: Richard Gardner/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Another eye-catching lot was number 219 – Wallace and Gromit’s nemesis, Feathers McGraw, disguised as a nun. The catalogue reminded bidders of one of the best Wallace and Gromit lines: “Feathers McGraw? Don’t be ridiculous. That’s just an innocent nun, out for a pleasure cruise.”
It was not only Wallace, Gromit and Feathers that proved popular. Aardman aficionados snapped up pieces related to the studio’s early days including clay puppets of Morph and his pal Chas.
Every lot started at £100 but as bidding got under way at tea time in London, it was clear they were not going to stay low for long.

The Morph and Chas puppets, made from Plasticine by Aardman co-founder Peter Lord and accompanied by handwritten care instructions, one of the first pieces to be auctioned, sold for £3,780 including buyer’s premium.

blocks.caption: Chas (L) and Morph. Photograph: Propstore

blocks.text: Mischievous Morph first appeared in 1977 as part of Take Hart, before starring in his own series of adventures. Another lot – lunch for six with Lord in Bristol – was bought by someone for more than £11,000.

Storyboards from Wallace & Gromit: The Wrong Trousers signed by another Aardman grandee, Nick Park, went for almost £4,000. A 9cm-tall clay rabbit that appeared in The Curse of the Were-Rabbit cost almost £10,000.

Bidders whose budget could not stretch to a Wallace or Gromit puppet could buy more modest souvenirs such as lot 89 – dry stone walls and gate from the Shaun the Sheep television series. That came with “adhesive remnants from where the pieces were secured to the set”.
The sale, run by the memorabilia auction house Propstore, marked the 50th anniversary of the Bristol-based studio, with the profits to be used to train new generations of animators.
Ngaio Harding-Hill, the director of attractions and live experiences and archive at Aardman, described it as an “unprecedented opportunity” to own a part of the studio’s 50-year history.
Harding-Hill said the collection had been carefully curated by the Aardman team to make sure the studio’s five decades were reflected in the auction.

She said: “Proceeds from the auction will be invested in talent development initiatives across Aardman, including bursaries at our world-class training facility, the Aardman Academy, meaning every sale is contributing to nurturing the next generation of animation talent.”

articles.title: House wraps up budget talks on more agencies
articles.summary: Budget deliberations for fiscal year 2027 of at least seven more agencies have been terminated by the House of Representatives, which is expected to finish such hearings this week before the General…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am

Among the agencies whose proposals and period of sponsorship and debate were finished were the Departments of Education (DepEd), Energy (DOE), Transportation (DOTr), Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), Civil Service Commission (CSC) and Commission on Higher Education (CHED).
Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Budget deliberations for fiscal year 2027 of at least seven more agencies have been terminated by the House of Representatives, which is expected to finish such hearings this week before the General Appropriations Bill is approved on second reading early next month.

DepEd’s budget allocation of P975.9 billion for next year under Secretary Sonny Angara got the House’s green light. This represents 13.55 percent of the proposed P7.2 trillion national budget for 2027, according to Rep. Maria Carmen Zamora.

“Once again, this single largest allocation of any department in the government as part of the education sector, is consistent with the mandate of the Constitution. It affirms that this House continues to treat education not as an expense but as the nation’s most important investment,” she said.

The House also terminated debates on DOE’s P5.58-billion allocation, DOTr’s P300.96 billion, DSWD’s P241.2 billion, ERC’s P944 million, independent constitutional CSC’s P4.04-billion budget as well as CHED’s P35.45-billion spending plans for next year.

DOE-ERC budget sponsor Rep. Arnie Fuentebella said the budget, including its attached agencies, is a forward-looking investment in the government’s capacity to ensure energy resilience amidst global uncertainties.
As for DOTr, Reps. Edwin Ongchuan and Reynante Arrogancia said the allocation is not only for infrastructure, but is also about making easier and efficient the travel time of the commuting public.

The P148.63-million 2027 budget of the Career Executive Service Board, which is under the CSC – has been approved, as lawmakers vow to support operations of human resource governance, professionalization, workplace cooperation and administrative justice.

articles.title: PSA: Bangsamoro polls random manual audit 99.9% accurate
articles.summary: The Random Manual Audit conducted for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary election yielded an overall accuracy rate of 99.99561 percent, based on the results from all 21…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am

Data from the PSA’s summary report on variance and accuracy rate showed that the audit covered 100 percent, or 21 out of 21, of the selected sample clustered precincts under the BARMM parliamentary polls.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Random Manual Audit conducted for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary election yielded an overall accuracy rate of 99.99561 percent, based on the results from all 21 BARMM sample clustered precincts audited as of Sept. 23, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority.
The audit found no variance between the automated election system (AES) results and the manual count for two of the three positions reviewed.

For the regional parliament political party race, the AES and manual audit both recorded 7,614 votes, resulting in an accuracy rate of 100 percent. Similarly, the AES and manual count for the member of parliament from the sectoral group for settler communities both tallied 12,006 votes, also posting an accuracy rate of 100 percent.

The only discrepancy was recorded in the district representative to the Bangsamoro parliament race, wherein the AES count showed 7,592 votes while the manual audit recorded 7,591 votes, reflecting a variance of one vote and an accuracy rate of 99.98683 percent.
The PSA reported that the overall variance across the audited positions amounted to a single vote.

The random manual audit is conducted to verify the accuracy of election returns generated by the automated election system by comparing them with manually counted ballots from randomly selected precincts.

The 80 winners in the Bangsamoro parliamentary polls will be formally sworn in on Oct. 30 and will later select the head of the regional government. Their mandate will cover a five-year period, with their term scheduled to conclude on June 30, 2031.
The BARMM conducted its inaugural parliamentary elections on Sept. 14, drawing 2,018,478 voters, or an equivalent of 84.34 percent of the region’s 2.393 million registered voters.

Meanwhile, President Marcos congratulated interim BARMM chief minister and Bangsamoro Federalist Party chairman Abdulraof Macacua for what the administration described as the “successful” conduct of the first parliamentary polls on Wednesday at Malacañang. – Alexis Romero

articles.title: Warships from ASEAN, other states sail in West Philippine Sea
articles.summary: Eleven warships from Association of Southeast Asian nations member states and other partner nations sailed the waters of the West Philippine Sea on Wednesday as part of this year’s ASEAN…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am

The Philippine Navy’s BRP Jose Rizal led the maritime activity off the coast of Zambales where the international event aimed at sustaining and strengthening regional security cooperation is being held.
Armed Forces of the Philippines

MANILA, Philippines — Eleven warships from Association of Southeast Asian nations member states and other partner nations sailed the waters of the West Philippine Sea (WPS) on Wednesday as part of this year’s ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) Experts’ Working Group on Maritime Security (EWG-MS).
Among the ASEAN warships that participated were the BRP Tarlac also from the Philippine Navy and one military vessel each for from Singapore and Brunei.
For the PLUS countries, India and New Zealand had two warships while Australia, the United States, and Japan sent one military vessel each.
The participating warships showcased various drill formations in the WPS, an activity that China did not participate in despite also being a PLUS-member state.

Reports said when a Chinese warship appeared from a distance apparently to monitor as the ASEAN-PLUS military vessels were sailing towards the exercise area near Panatag (Scarborough) Shoal or Bajo de Masinloc within the Philippine exclusive economic zone (EEZ).
The Philippine Navy communicated with it through radio, welcoming and inviting it to join but received no response.

Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. led the official opening of the ADMM-Plus EWG-MS with a Joint Cooperative Activity (JCA) and Future Leaders’ Program (FLP) last Monday in Olongapo City, Zambales.

Co-hosted by the Philippines and Japan, the activity will feature a series of harbor and sea phase activities involving personnel, naval assets, ships and aircraft from eight ADMM-Plus countries from Sept. 20 to 26 with observers from fellow ASEAN member states and dialogue partners.

“We hope that this exercise will be foundational in two things: number one, learning the procedures or getting familiar with the procedures and working together and cooperation; and secondly, develop, at an early stage, networking, trust and cooperation amongst all the participants and your respective defense establishments and navies,” Teodoro said.

“Our collaboration and cooperation not merely in response but in early prepositioning, working together and in detection becomes more critical,” he stressed, adding that an important avenue for effective and efficient response are free open sea lanes of communication.

The Philippine Navy earlier announced that as co-chairs of the EWG on MS for the 2024–2027 cycle, the Philippines and Japan will lead the two engagements which will bring together participating navies from ASEAN Member States and Plus partner countries to advance practical cooperation and strengthen maritime security collaboration.

“The JCA will be conducted in two phases: the Harbor/Shore Phase and the At-Sea Phase. It will feature cooperative activities designed to strengthen practical maritime security cooperation and confidence-building among participating navies,” it said.

articles.title: Monsod criticizes senators over stand on vote threshold
articles.summary: A framer of the 1987 Constitution called out Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Camille Villar, who objected to the proposal to lower the number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — A framer of the 1987 Constitution called out Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Camille Villar, who objected to the proposal to lower the number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial.

Former Commission on Elections (Comelec) chairman Christian Monsod, who helped craft the 1987 Constitution, said Cayetano and Villar may be wrong in challenging the majority ruling of the Senate impeachment court.

Cayetano and Villar were among the six senators who boycotted the voting to modify the original threshold of 16 out of the 24 senators set by impeachment trial presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero.
Excluded in the voting on Wednesday were senators who are facing charges, detained, in hiding or on sick leave even if the two-thirds threshold mandated by the 1987 Constitution remained.
Thirteen senators voted in favor of the motion – stating that 14 votes out of 20 senators are needed for a conviction – while one, Escudero, was against. Six others did not participate in the voting.

Cayetano tried but failed to block the proposal, arguing that a vote to favor lowering the number of senators qualified to vote to convict or acquit could violate the provision in the 1987 Constitution that requires “No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate” in an impeachment trial.
When asked about Cayetano’s argument in an interview over radio dzBB yesterday, Monsod said, “He’s wrong.”
Monsod said the Senate can continue the impeachment trial against Duterte amid plans by some senators to boycott the proceedings.
“As long as there is a quorum, the Senate can continue. If they plan on doing that (boycott), it’s for headlines only. They talk like they know everything, especially Cayetano,” he said.

Monsod took a swipe at Villar’s opinion seeking respect for their colleagues currently being detained. She turned emotional in defending her fellow senators whom she said have not been convicted of the charges pressed against them.
“She does not understand the law,” he said.

Monsod noticed the difference in views of Camille and her brother Sen. Mark Villar, who voted to adjust the denominator in the voting threshold. “I don’t know whether they are playing the political game.”

Meanwhile, Monsod maintained the Anti-Plunder Act or Republic Act 7080 explicitly mandates that government officials charged with plunder shall be suspended from exercising the functions of their office.

In addition, the lowering of what he called the “denominator” in the voting threshold should also include a “fugitive from justice because once he is arrested, he is already prevented from exercising his power.”

The 24-member Senate is currently down to 20 with the absence of detained Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, both facing plunder and graft charges, and Sen. Ronald dela Rosa who remains in hiding while facing arrest by the International Criminal Court (ICC).

On Sen. Loren Legarda, who is on a prolonged medical leave, Monsod said: “We will see whether she should be included in the denominator or not… because she participated in the deliberations before she left for that leave.”
In recalling how the 1987 Constitution was created, Monsod said they changed the provision on the voting threshold in an impeachment trial from three-fourths to two-thirds.
He also believed the Supreme Court (SC) “should not interfere in the definition of the powers” of the Senate, which creates its own rules.
Not indicative of guilty verdict
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said the 13 votes to lower the conviction threshold was not indicative of the verdict in the Vice President’s impeachment trial.
In a chance interview yesterday, Gatchalian denied that the 13 votes were “reflective” of the verdict, adding that the senators will decide based on the evidence presented during the trial.
“No. Because when it comes to the verdict, it’s about the evidence, it’s about the testimonies, it’s about how the prosecution and defense will present their cases,” said Gatchalian.
“The defense is trying to prove that the allegations have no basis. It’s complicated. We have yet to reach the final voting,” Gatchalian said.
Asked if the outcome of the threshold voting meant that the numbers were enough to convict, Gatchalian said: “Nothing is certain.”
Airtight evidence

House prosecutors vowed to do their best in persuading senators to convict the Vice President based on the airtight evidence they will present moving forward and regardless of the final voting threshold.

“We are not here to count the votes, we are not vote-counters here. We have to present the evidence needed to convict the VP based on the Articles of Impeachment that we have filed,” Rep. Terry Ridon, a member of the House prosecution team, said.
Lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro said it’s still a long way to go before the senators cast their votes. – Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Delon Porcalla

articles.title: DepEd: Schools’ budget doubled in 5 years
articles.summary: The budget for public schools has doubled in five years, from P30 The budget for public schools has doubled in five years, from P30 billion in 2022 to P61.02 billion in the proposed 2027 budget, the…

This file photo shows a facade of the Department of Education.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The budget for public schools has doubled in five years, from P30 billion in 2022 to P61.02 billion in the proposed 2027 budget, the Department of Education said yesterday.
Included in the DepEd’s P975.96-billion budget for 2027 is the increase in school-level maintenance and other operating expenses (MOOE).
Per-learner MOOE allocations for elementary schools will reach P2,982; junior high school, P2,744 and senior high school, P3,558. This year’s school operating funds are at P60.89 billion.

“By simplifying funding formulas and steadily expanding per-learner operational support, we are removing unnecessary bottlenecks so school administrators and teachers can focus on teaching rather than worrying about basic school upkeep,” Education Secretary Sonny Angara said.
Critics have slammed the lower budget for education in the 2027 national outlay compared to this year.

articles.title: NBI: 1 contractor bagged P7 billion Davao flood projects
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation is looking into a much larger pool of Davao infrastructure contracts than previously disclosed, with a preliminary Commission on Audit (COA) report putting the…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is looking into a much larger pool of Davao infrastructure contracts than previously disclosed, with a preliminary Commission on Audit (COA) report putting the value at about P7 billion for 51 projects awarded to one contractor from 2018 to 2024.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the figure surfaced as the bureau reviewed documents in its investigation of alleged irregularities in flood control projects in Davao City.

The amount is significantly higher than the previously reported P1.9 billion worth of projects awarded to Genesis88 Construction Inc. in the district of Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte. The NBI has identified 47 projects for closer examination, with six initially described as clearly questionable based on the documents reviewed.
“The initial report we received from COA was P7 billion,” Matibag said over dzRH on Thursday. “One contractor had P7 billion worth of projects, with 51 projects.”

The contracts span from 2018 to 2024, although Matibag said the bulk of the projects were awarded from 2022 to 2024. The NBI is now examining why one contractor repeatedly secured projects and whether the bidding and procurement processes were properly followed.

Matibag said the bureau would also consult the Philippine Competition Commission to determine whether the pattern of contracts raised competition concerns. “There are many contractors. Why is it that only one or two repeatedly receive the contracts?” he said.
The NBI had earlier reported possible ghost and substandard projects, as well as projects appearing to have the same coordinates but different titles and separate budgets.

Matibag said officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) were being asked to explain the projects and provide supporting records, while the NBI would formally seek additional documents from COA.
The bureau has already identified the owners of the construction companies involved and plans to summon them as the investigation progresses.

Matibag stressed that the investigation is not directed at any particular politician and that receiving projects in a congressional district does not by itself establish wrongdoing by the lawmaker representing it.
“What we will first look at is the bidding process,” he said. “It does not automatically mean that a person is criminally involved or conspired in wrongdoing.”

The NBI director said investigators would need evidence of intervention or participation in the procurement process before linking any public official to possible criminal liability. He added the bureau would continue examining projects regardless of the political affiliation of officials involved.
Matibag noted the investigation remains ongoing and that the documents and testimony being gathered will determine whether criminal charges should be filed.
DPWH Davao chief appears before NBI

DPWH Region XI Director Juby Cordon appeared before the NBI on Thursday to comply with a subpoena issued in connection with the bureau’s probe into alleged irregularities in flood control projects in Davao.
Cordon arrived at the NBI headquarters in Pasay City at around 1 p.m. but declined to answer questions from reporters.
Ten boxes of documents from DPWH Region XI were also brought to the NBI as the bureau examines around 50 flood control projects flagged for possible irregularities.
Cordon was subpoenaed to provide records covering 37 contracts, most of them in Davao City and Davao del Sur.
The subpoena, issued on Sept. 17, cited possible violations of the Revised Penal Code on malversation, the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act and the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

Matibag earlier said the bureau found red flags in 47 of 100 projects reviewed based on DPWH records. Six of the 47 were initially identified as clearly questionable, including projects suspected to be ghost or substandard and those that appeared to carry different titles and funding despite having the same coordinates.

articles.title: Suspects linked to school shooting, online grooming nabbed
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation has apprehended a person connected to the Sept. 18 school shooting incident in South Cotabato, the third such incident to hit the country’s schools in just…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am
Education officials inspected on Saturday the scene of the deadly gun attack. the day before, inside the Banga National High School campus in Banga, South Cotabato.
Philstar.com / John Unson

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has apprehended a person connected to the Sept. 18 school shooting incident in South Cotabato, the third such incident to hit the country’s schools in just three months.

During the Department of Justice (DOJ) budget hearing at the Senate yesterday, NBI Director Melvin Matibag mentioned the developments in the bureau’s probe on the latest school shooting incident at Banga National High School that left three students dead, including the 14-year-old shooter who was allegedly influenced by the nihilistic violent extremist (NVE) network “True Crime Community.”
Matibag said that the NBI is monitoring the deep dark web and investigating NVE cases behind the grooming of the teen school shooters in Tacloban, Zamboanga City and South Cotabato.
“We’re doing our best to monitor it. And incidentally, I may report, yesterday we were able to get hold of one of the individuals somehow related to what happened in South Cotabato,” Matibag said.
The NBI also apprehended a suspected “groomer” in Cebu, Matibag said, without explaining if the person is connected to any of the three school shooting incidents.

“Yesterday also, we made an apprehension of one of suspected groomers from Cebu, and with the help of the Department of Justice National Prosecution Service, we will be processing it today,” Matibag said.

Matibag appealed for the Senate to consider increasing up to P1 billion their proposed P175 million confidential fund allocation in their proposed 2027 budget, so that the NBI can procure equipment to crack down on cybercrime offenses, like digital fraud and nihilistic violence targeting vulnerable youth.
“There is really an NVE group, and there are lurkers that are copying this. It can be as simple as a student that did not do his homework saying that there will be a shooting,” Matibag said.
“So those are the things that we want to monitor as a team. The NBI, we want to be very active on this one,” he added.
Matibag said that the NBI will submit to Congress their proposals for a possible law to regulate and monitor social media through “age-gating.”

“So it depends on the age, on who will be allowed and how they will be allowed to use… Then coordination with the school, the threat validation and school response, which we did. We were able to apprehend this personality from South Cotabato because of the assistance of the schools involved in what we are doing,” the NBI chief said.

articles.title: 40 Philippines seafarers safe after Singapore Strait collision

This photo taken on April 21, 2026, shows vessels in the Singapore straits.

MANILA, Philippines — About 40 Filipino seafarers on Panama-flagged bulk carrier First Margaux were confirmed safe after it collided with a China-registered fishing vessel in the Singapore Strait.
None of the Filipino crew members were reported injured, Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said yesterday.
The Department of Migrant Workers is still gathering information from the vessel’s manning agency.
The DMW is coordinating with the families of affected seafarers and will provide aid as needed.
First Margaux collided with Lu Qing Yuan Yu on Sept. 17, the Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) of Singapore said.

“The vessel was subsequently towed to Raffles Reserved Anchorage for assessment. “There were no reported injuries among the crew of either vessel or pollution arising from the incident. Navigational traffic was not affected,” it added.

articles.title: ADB approves $1.5 billion Philippines crisis response loan
articles.summary: The Asian Development Bank has approved a $1.5-billion loan to help the Philippines address the impact of the Middle East conflict.

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 12:00am
In a statement yesterday, the multilateral lender said that the loan will be used to help finance the government’s Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food and Transport program.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a $1.5-billion loan to help the Philippines address the impact of the Middle East conflict.
Under UPLIFT, the government is providing financial support to low-income Filipinos affected by rising fuel prices stemming from the Middle East conflict.

Measures include fare discounts, fuel and fertilizer subsidies, as well as medical packages and cash assistance for poor and vulnerable households, public transport operators and drivers, small-scale farmers and fisherfolk.

Apart from helping the government secure fuel supplies and keeping power, health services, food and medicines affordable, the ADB’s support will also be used to provide assistance to returning overseas Filipino workers (OFWs).
The financing will be coming from ADB’s Countercyclical Support Facility, a region-wide crisis financing mechanism.
“Every week this crisis continues to ask more of people who have little left to give,” ADB President Masato Kanda said.

“They have a right to expect that the institutions serving them will meet their struggle with equal resolve. With this financing, we are backing the Philippines’ determination to keep its people secure and its future within its own hands,” he added.
Last May, Kanda offered $1.75 billion in additional support to President Marcos to help the Philippines respond to the impact of the Middle East tensions on the economy.
As the impact of the Middle East conflict widened the government’s financing needs, the ADB raised the loan amount for an existing health care program last month.
In particular, the ADB raised the loan amount for the Build Universal Health Care Program Subprogram 3 by $250 million, bringing the total financing to $750 million.
Given the Philippines’ reliance on imports for its fuel and fertilizer needs, the country is vulnerable to sharp increases in global prices.
The Middle East conflict has also affected the Philippine economy as the region serves as a major destination for OFWs.
About 1.1 million OFWs were deployed in the Middle East last year. These workers accounted for about 18 percent of the country’s $35.6 billion in total remittances in 2025.
Amid surging fuel prices, the De- partment of Finance has endorsed the suspension of the excise tax on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene, but not on diesel and gasoline.

articles.title: Reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways rise by fifth in a year
articles.summary:
Unions say record high of nearly 25,000, including assaults on rail workers and public, shows need for more staff and policing

The number of reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways has…

blocks.text: The number of reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways has risen by a fifth to a record high of almost 25,000 incidents in a year.

Unions said the “horrendous” figures showed the need for more staff and policing, as the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) revealed a sharp increase in assaults on the travelling public and on railway staff last year.

There were 13,464 reported assaults against passengers and members of the public on the mainline railway in 2025-26, up 36% on the previous year and the highest number recorded by the ORR since it started tracking the figures in 2004.
Assaults on rail staff were up 12% in a year to 11,289 reported incidents, mainly verbal abuse but including nearly 2,500 physical assaults – an average of about seven every day.
The assaults on members of the public included startling rises in cases of harassment, up 52% year on year, and common assault, up by 30%.

The figures partly reflect increased reporting and zero-tolerance campaigns on public transport, but also underline concerns flagged by unions about the threats to frontline workers as well as passengers, and the availability of transport police.

The RMT general secretary, Eddie Dempsey, said the numbers were horrendous but chimed with the union’s own surveys showing two-thirds of its members had experienced some form of violence at work in the past year.

He said: “We are calling for a significant increase in staffing across public transport, including an end to lone working. We also clearly need stronger legal protections for public transport workers against assaults at work.
“British Transport Police funding cuts have also been disastrous which has undermined a proper policing presence on all public transport.”

The TSSA union’s general secretary, Maryam Eslamdoust, said: “These new figures are shocking but not surprising because we have been warning for many months that violence on the railways is spiralling out of control.”
The government said it was increasing police funding and taking the issue “extremely seriously”.

A Department for Transport spokesperson said: “The rise in assaults on the railway is deeply concerning and completely unacceptable. No passenger or rail worker should face violence, threats or abuse, and we encourage anyone affected to report incidents to the police.
“The government and rail industry are taking this extremely seriously, with a £63m increase in British Transport Police funding by 2028-29, which will see over 200 additional officers recruited.”
New measures called railway behaviour notices were introduced in June 2026, strengthening the railway’s ability to exclude repeat offenders from stations.

BTP said they had been encouraging greater reporting of all types of assault by staff and passengers, including record use of the 61016 discreet text-to-report number, which partly explained the growing numbers.

Nonetheless, the BTP assistant chief constable said: “These figures are a stark reminder of the violence and abuse rail workers face simply for doing their jobs. We will never tolerate violence or abuse directed at passengers or staff on the railway, and anyone committing these crimes can expect a robust response from us.
“We remain committed to driving down these offences and ensuring the network is safe for everyone.”
after newsletter promotion
The chief inspector of railways, the ORR’s Richard Hines, said the increase in reported assaults was concerning, adding: “No one on the railway should be subjected to violence, threats or abuse.”
He said the ORR had set out guidance for employers on the risks, effective controls and encouraging staff to report incidents.

blocks.caption: The RMT is calling for increased rail staffing, including an end to lone working, and stronger legal protections for public transport workers.  Photograph: Murdo MacLeod/The Guardian

blocks.text: A spokesperson for Network Rail and train operators said: “Violence, abuse and intimidation directed at passengers or staff are completely unacceptable. The rail industry works closely with British Transport Police to investigate incidents, support victims and bring offenders to justice.”
They said the numbers also reflected greater intelligence sharing, improved reporting processes, and more CCTV and body-worn cameras for frontline staff.

The ORR report noted that the headline numbers of reported assaults can include multiple counts in a single incident, for example for both harassment and common assault, while workforce assaults are now recorded even if no physical injury occurs. On the London Underground, where there is single counting, the number of assaults on the workforce fell slightly last year.

The chief executive of the Rail Safety and Standards Board, Mark Phillips, said the rail industry was taking action to better protect staff, but the figures “underline the need for a change in public behaviour and greater respect for the people who keep the railway running safely every day”.

Reports in recent years have highlighted that women and girls were at particular risk, while the growing number of assaults year on year since the pandemic has coincided with pressure on British Transport Police numbers.

The abuse and intimidation faced by frontline staff on the railways has also been seen in sectors including retail and in the NHS. The British Retail Consortium warned over “endemic” violence towards shop workers earlier this year, while the number of reports of violence against NHS staff by patients surpassed 100,000 in 2025.

articles.title: CEO who posted about wearing 'Lake America' sweatshirts to Halifax is no longer CEO
articles.summary: The Michigan tourist who recently went viral over a Facebook photo where she and three family members appeared to be wearing "Lake America" sweatshirts has parted ways with her employer.

image.caption: A map labelling Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' is displayed in the White House after U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order to change its name on Aug. 27. (Jim Watson/AFP/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Canada
The Michigan tourist who recently went viral over a Facebook photo where she and three family members appeared to be wearing "Lake America" sweatshirts has parted ways with her employer.
Jane Smith no longer working for Michigan's Family First Credit Union
Jane Smith, the former CEO of Family First Credit Union in Saginaw, is no longer employed there, according to a statement posted on Wednesday to the company's website.

"We are reaching out to inform you that Jane Smith is no longer an employee of Family First Credit Union, effective immediately," reads the statement addressed to "Family First Credit Union Members and Community" and signed by the chair of the board of directors.

The statement continues to say that chief operations officer Jason Acosta is now serving as interim CEO. It does not provide any further information about why Smith is no longer employed, or whether the decision to leave the company was hers.

CBC News has reached out to Smith, Acosta and the credit union's marketing team, and not yet heard back. But the company apologized in a statement posted to the Family First Credit Union Facebook page on Wednesday.
"We sincerely apologize for the concern, disappointment and pain this situation has caused our members and community," the post reads.

"We understand that members of our community may hold different perspectives about this decision. Our responsibility is to act in the best interest of the Credit Union, uphold the trust of our members and continue putting our community first."
'Like our sweatshirts?'

The news comes in the wake of the backlash over a photo Smith had posted to Facebook on her way to Halifax, in which she and three family members pose wearing "Lake America" sweatshirts that Smith later said were AI-generated.
"Like our sweatshirts? Not sure Canada will," said the Sept. 11 photo originally posted by Smith, and later shared by her sister, followed by "lol lol."

items: Michigan tourist who posted about wearing 'Lake America' sweatshirts to Halifax says it was AI
'Lake America' change highlights Canada's reliance on U.S. tech

blocks.text: Judging by the reaction online, just weeks after U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" amid the trade war between the two countries, Canadians were not lol-ing.
In a previous interview with ABC12 News in Michigan, Smith said the image was AI-generated and meant to be a joke.
Republican mayor rejects Trump's Lake Ontario name change
"We weren't trying to make a political statement," Smith told the news outlet.
"However, we were, you know, kind of poking fun at the fact that, you know, one of the Great Lakes's names were getting changed."
She further explained that the sweatshirts weren't real, saying she ran a photo of them through ChatGPT to add the "Lake America" gear, then posted it to her private Facebook page with an AI label.
When they arrived in Halifax, it was her sister who reposted it publicly, added the comment and didn't include the AI warning, Smith said.
"We never had actual sweatshirts. We never wore sweatshirts."

There's been ongoing backlash over Trump's proposed name-change on both sides of the border. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said Canadians will call it Lake Ontario "now and always." In the U.S., three members of Congress have introduced a bill aimed at stopping Trump's renaming, titled "Hands off our Great Lakes."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Natalie Stechyson has been a writer and editor at CBC News since 2021. She covers stories on social trends, families, gender, human interest, as well as general news. She's worked as a journalist since 2009, with stints at the Globe and Mail and Postmedia News, among others. Before joining CBC News, she was the parents editor at HuffPost Canada, where she won a silver Canadian Online Publishing Award for her work on pregnancy loss. You can reach her at natalie.stechyson@cbc.ca.

articles.title: At Trump meeting, Xi Jingping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict
articles.summary: Chinese president’s proposals for lessening tensions come amid period of intense competition between the two countries over AI and trade

blocks.text: Xi Jingping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put the US and China on a military collision course.

At the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House, the Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could avoid military conflict between the two competing superpowers.

“We should strengthen communication. China and the United States are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialog, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust,” said Xi, with Trump looking on.

“We should coexist in peace,” he said. “China and the United States, as two major countries, stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation. Our two militaries should maintain regular dialog and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention.”

With such conditions in place, Xi said, “the Thucydides trap can be overcome”, refering to the phenomenon, defined by the Greek historian, of tensions that arise when an emerging power challenges the dominance of an established power.
Xi invoked the phrase in his meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, asking the US president how he planned to avoid it.

His proposals for lessening tensions – which also included the invitation of 100,000 young Americans to visit China on student exchanges – come amid a period of intense competition between the two powers over artificial intelligence and trade, with each side imposing tariffs on the other.

Trump had earlier welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to the White House, noting that he was the first Chinese leader to make a second state visit to the US. The previous visit occurred in 2015, when Barack Obama was US president.

Trump declared that he had forged “a truly great friendship” with Xi. “President Xi and I have made tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries,” he said. “Our teams have been working to encourage a more balances trading relationship, including the new market access for American farmers and ranchers.”

He said the current visit would include discussion overs security, technology and AI – which he called “super intelligence”, a term he introduced in his speech to the United Nations general assembly on Tuesday.

Scheme set up after Russian invasion in 2022 paid £350 a month to people hosting Ukrainians but this will reduce to £100 next year

Ukrainian refugees fear they could be left homeless after…

blocks.text: Ukrainian refugees fear they could be left homeless after the government quietly axed 70% of funding for hosts of the Homes for Ukraine scheme, reducing monthly “thank you” payments to them from £350 to £100.
The scheme was launched after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has provided support for 181,000 of the 234,000 Ukrainians who have since sought sanctuary in the UK.

Now the government has said it will cut the hosting payments and reduce contributions to local authorities which are paid a sum for each arrival to meet costs associated with the delivery of the programme.

A written statement to parliament from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government on 15 September said funding would be reduced from £5,900 to £3,300. The changes will come into effect from 1 January 2027.

Tetiana, a 73-year-old Ukrainian refugee who has been hosted for two years and four months, said she was devastated to read the government’s letter circulated to hosts in the last few days informing them of the changes.

“I feel that this financial change could impact on my host’s ability to host me. If the hosting comes to an end I don’t know where I will go and how I can start again. I can’t work because of my age and because I have mobility problems. I fled from Kharkiv which is close to the Russia frontline so I can’t go back to Ukraine. I don’t know what I will do. I’m at a loss about what my options will be. This change has created a lot of uncertainty for me. I don’t know how I would be able to pay rent if hosting finishes for me.”

Nataliya Rumyanetseva is hosting her mother, the first Ukrainian to arrive in the UK after the war started. She said the changes were likely to have a significant impact. “When refugees arrive here from Ukraine they are shell shocked and need time to adapt and learn the language. If hosting changes to become a more commercial rental arrangement I think that’s cruel.”

One host who lives in Greenwich said he did not know if he would be able to continue hosting because of the drop in payments. “I’ve been a sponsor since May 2022. I was dismayed to learn that thank you payments are reducing to just £100. I lost my job within months of becoming a sponsor and these payments have become an absolute lifeline even though I did not volunteer for this scheme for the money. I genuinely worry about the consequences of this change for Ukrainians in the UK.”
One option the government proposes is that hosts can switch to landlord status and charge refugees rent.

A host who lives in Cardiff and is hosting a Ukrainian who has enrolled on a course of study said: “The situation feels like a cheap shot from the government. We, in good faith, opened our home to someone in need. That person, in good faith, planned for a life in the UK. And the government in what seems like very bad faith, saw an easy way to claw money back from people who aren’t in a position to stop them.”
The government says it has so far provided more than £1.81bn for the scheme.
The Home Office has been approached for comment.

The lifting of the ban came after the CICC and Discord management’s meeting earlier to discuss compliance matters.
Paraiso said Discord has committed to give the agency a “green lane” to monitor and recognize threat actors in its platform.
The platform was also given the choice to either establish a local satellite office or send representatives in the country for ease of communication and coordination.

The CICC on Tuesday gave both Reddit and Discord 24 hours to establish a Philippine presence within 24 hours to enhance collaboration with the government following the shooting at the Banga National High School in South Cotabato.
DICT Secretary Henry Aguda announced that Discord already committed to strengthen its child protection measures in the platform.
“They also recognized and acknowledged na merong kailangan ayusin at paghigpitan sa kanilang mga polisiya (their policies need fixing and be stricter),” Aguda said. —RF, GMA News

Alake said the agreement, which was signed on Wednesday, would be used to identify viable projects. He hinted that local jobs could be created by onshoring the refining of minerals, which until now have largely been exported as ore.

However, these goals come as Nigeria's mining sector remains mired by safety concerns and environmental concerns.

articles.title: Rick Wakeman performs piano concert to 150 rescued moon bears in Vietnam
articles.summary:
Former Yes musician plays at sanctuary to raise awareness of animals that remain stuck in cages at ‘bile farms’

Rick Wakeman has played to all kinds of people around the globe, but he has…

blocks.text: Rick Wakeman has played to all kinds of people around the globe, but he has now performed to an audience he had never encountered before – an enclosure of 150 bears.
The former Yes musician, who has gone on to have a prolific solo career, played the piano at a Vietnamese bear sanctuary.

“Before you ask, I won’t be playing the teddy bear’s picnic,” he joked ahead of the performance. Wakeman, who is a supporter of animal welfare causes and has rescue dogs and cats of his own, is conducting the concert to raise awareness of moon bears kept in cruel conditions for the extraction of their bile.

He said he was a bit worried about how hot it is going to be. “You know the heatwave we had in England? It’s double that,” he said. “They offered to rig up a fan for me, but I figured that will just blow more hot air around.”

blocks.caption: A moon bear at the bear sanctuary in Tam Dao national park, Vietnam. Photograph: Luong Thai Linh/EPA

blocks.text: His concert was performed live on a Yamaha grand piano positioned in Animals Asia’s bear sanctuary in the Tam Dao national park, and Wakeman had written some new compositions especially for rescued bears.

Asked whether the bears would enjoy the music, he said: “They’ve not got much choice, really. It’s a well-known fact that all animals react to music, especially gentle melodic music. So what I am going to do is piano music that is melodic, and I can only hope that they will come up to the perimeter of the sanctuary and have a listen.”

blocks.caption: Rick Wakeman plays piano at bear sanctuary

blocks.text: Wakeman has been sponsoring rescue bears since 2016 and recently adopted a new one: “He’s only 20 months old, a big fella, I went to see him today. He came out right to the edge and stood on his back legs and just stared at me, it was brilliant.”

Bile is extracted from bears for traditional Chinese medicine by putting a needle into their gall bladder and drawing it out. The bears are kept in poor conditions in countries including China and in Vietnam, where it has just been banned, but where some bears are still in captivity in cramped enclosures. It is the fourth-biggest market in the illegal wildlife trade in east Asia, resulting in a dramatic decline in the Asiatic black bear populations in Vietnam, with nearly a third of their numbers lost around the world in just 30 years.

blocks.caption: Wakeman performing for the rescued bears. Photograph: Luong Thai Linh/EPA

blocks.text: Of the sanctuary, which he has been visiting this week, Wakeman said: “To see the bears be rehabilitated, having a life they never had before, some have never put their feet on grass before. They are so wonderful, that we can do such horrendous things to animals is beyond belief. Before this, they were chained in cages sometimes for 10 or 20 years in conditions where they couldn’t even turn around.”

He is playing to raise awareness for the bears still stuck in cages in Vietnam and to urge the government to get them released: “We have 150 bears at the sanctuary, but there are 125 bears left in cages in the old bear bile farms, and there are four dying a month. We have to get them out quick and into the sanctuary.”

He treats his rescue dogs and cats to music back at home in Suffolk. “I had one cat who used to jump on the grand piano, and if I stopped playing he would put his paw in the strings and rattle them until I played again. I know if my dogs don’t like it, they will get up and walk out, and my cats don’t like metal, grunge or rap. They want a melody.”

blocks.caption: Bears playing at the sanctuary. Photograph: Luong Thai Linh/EPA

blocks.text: Wakeman spends hours watching the bears. “If you see these bears it is hard to put into words, they are almost human the way they look at you,” he said. “If you see them, you can’t help but be moved. They aren’t tame but they are very safe, very happy, they play, they romp. I witnessed two today jumping in a bubble bath and playing. They’ve got a life back.”

Dr Jill Robinson, the founder and CEO of Animals Asia, said: “We are beyond blessed to have Rick’s support for Animals Asia and the bears. His love for them is immeasurable and can be heard in the beautifully haunting music he has written for them. We’re all so excited to hear his performance in the open air at our sanctuary in the stunning setting of Tam Dao national park. I can’t wait to see how the bears respond.”
Wakeman added: “I hope they lay down and have a listen, that would make my day. I would have a big grin on my face.”

articles.title: Palestinian president, denied visa to speak at UN, addresses leaders in pre-recorded video
articles.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN General Assembly on Thursday, delivering pre-recorded remarks from his office in Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top…

image.caption: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly via pre-recorded video in New York City on Thursday. (Mike Segar/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN General Assembly on Thursday, delivering pre-recorded remarks from his office in Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top Palestinian officials visas to attend the gathering for the second year in a row.
Israel's Netanyahu will speak in person on Thursday afternoon

"The Palestinian people face one of the most dangerous times in its history," Abbas said, citing long-term military occupation in the West Bank and the war in Gaza. Israel, he said, "has targeted all of the basic necessities of life."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was scheduled to speak in person early in the afternoon. As Abbas spoke, the Israeli delegations' seats in the General Assembly hall sat vacant.
In his speech, Abbas once again implored the international community to take more vigorous action and speak out more loudly against Israel.

"How much longer will some states continue to remain silent against Israel or supply it with the weapons it uses against our people? The world has witnessed the tremendous cost in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank," Abbas said. "What is the international community waiting for in order to protect the Palestinian people?"

Though negotiations have not taken place for years, Abbas urged the international community to push for a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Netanyahu has said no Palestinian state will be established while he is Israel's leader and has argued that the Palestinian Authority is not a partner for peace.
Israel set to oust Palestinians from Gaza if U.S. signs off, defence minister says

The international community has backed U.S. President Donald Trump's plan for a group of apolitical administrators to govern Gaza under the Board of Peace. But Abbas said the territory could not remain politically separate from the West Bank and East Jerusalem for the long term.
He said the Gaza Strip, East Jerusalem and the West Bank needed to be governed by "one state, one government, one law and one legitimate entity authorized to bear arms."
Abbas recorded the video on Wednesday.

Since 2005, the now-90-year-old Abbas has led the Palestinian Authority, which is the internationally recognized representative of the Palestinian people. But his support among Palestinians has withered during years of corruption and the sometimes-violent advance of Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Under Abbas, Palestine has been recognized as a country by a majority of UN member states. But on the ground in the West Bank, the mostly symbolic moves have not affected Israel's decades-long military occupation. Throughout the war in Gaza, Abbas and the authority have been largely sidelined from negotiations over its future in favour of a transition process shepherded by the U.S.-backed Board of Peace.

items: Trump's 'Board of Peace' earmarks $2.45B US in blueprint to rebuild war-torn Gaza
Canada pledges $100M for Palestine at United Nations General Assembly

blocks.text: The Palestinian Authority was created under a series of peace agreements with Israel in the 1990s and administers semi-autonomous areas of the West Bank, while relying heavily on foreign aid.

It was ousted from Gaza after Hamas won parliamentary elections in 2006 and violently seized control. Abbas was elected to what was supposed to be a four-year term in 2005. The authority has not held presidential or legislative elections since 2006.

Israel captured the West Bank and East Jerusalem in the 1967 war, and the Palestinians want both as part of their future state. The Palestinians and much of the international community view the settlements as illegal and as an obstacle to creating a viable, contiguous Palestinian state.

items: Alex Eala suffered a surprising defeat to world No. 180 Tatiana Prozorova in the round of 16 at the Singapore Open, marking her first loss to a player outside the top 100 since November 2025.
Eala had a strong start, leading 4-2 in the second set, but ultimately lost the match after dropping 11 of the final 15 games.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala used to be the one pulling off upsets, but on Thursday, September 24, she found herself on the receiving end.

Eala suffered a surprise exit from the Singapore Open after a stunning 4-6, 7-5, 6-3 defeat to world No. 180 Tatiana Prozorova of Russia in the round of 16 at Centre Court of the OCBC Arena on Thursday, September 24.
Seeded second, Eala looked poised to reach the quarterfinals after racing to a 4-2 lead in the second set, only to drop 11 of the final 15 games as Prozorova secured the biggest win of her career.
The loss marked the first time Eala, currently the world No. 18, lost to a player ranked outside the top 100 since she broke into the top 50 in November 2025.
Most of the fans who packed Centre Court expected Eala to cruise to the last eight, especially after she reached the third round of the US Open earlier this September.

And Prozorova’s track record hardly hinted at her capacity for a shocker as she was making her first appearance in the round of 16 of a WTA 500 tournament. She has also made a Grand Slam main draw just once.
The 22-year-old Russian, however, defied the odds.
“Wow, I just did it,” said Prozorova. “I just believed in myself ’til the end. I knew that she will fight. I will also fight ’til the end. That was what I did and it worked.”

Eala even grabbed a 3-2 lead in the deciding set after breaking Prozorova, but the Russian hit her stride and reeled off the next four games to earn the right to face China’s Wang Xinyu in the quarterfinals.
Prozorova fired 52 winners, including a forehand that sailed past Eala and wrapped up the marathon match in 3 hours and 9 minutes.
Coming off a two-week break after the US Open, Eala produced just 24 winners, although she tallied fewer unforced errors, 52-63.
Eala can shift her focus to the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, where she is expected to contend for the women’s singles crown following her bronze finish in the 2023 edition in Hangzhou, China.

With the likes of world No. 1 Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan, No. 17 Naomi Osaka of Japan, and defending champion Zheng Qinwen of China skipping the continental showpiece, Eala enters the tournament as a leading contender for the gold medal. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Australia’s newest chicken factory looks like a modern art gallery – but will it improve animal welfare?
articles.summary:
Three million chickens a week will be processed at the state-of-the-art facility in Tamworth – a fifth of all those eaten nationwide

It is for birds? Is it for planes?

The sleek,…

blocks.text: It is for birds? Is it for planes?

The sleek, rust-coloured saucer settles into the earth, mirroring the surrounding hills. It looks like an art gallery or a high-end conference centre – an architectural masterpiece designed to sit lightly on the land.
Until you see the shed behind it.
The sweeping lines are the gateway to a $600m poultry processing plant that will, at full capacity, process 3 million chickens a week.

Located in Tamworth, 300km north of Sydney, the new facility is owned by Baiada, one of Australia’s two largest chicken producers and the owner of household brand names Steggles and Lilydale Free Range.

blocks.caption: Workers at the new plant can spend their lunch breaks at an on-site cafeteria, at a gym or in landscaped gardens. Photograph: Baiada

blocks.text: At its height, two lines will process 15,000 birds an hour as chickens fly through state-of-the-art chilling systems and automated packing machines en route to supermarkets across the state. The new plant will support more than 1,000 jobs, with workers able to spend their lunch breaks at an on-site cafeteria, at a gym or in landscaped gardens.

Jeff Budd, deputy mayor of Tamworth regional council, has toured the facility, which opened last week. He says the unusual design creates a gem for the city and will attract the skilled workers and technicians needed to run kilometres’ worth of conveyor belts and systems.
“I think it’s massive for the entire region,” he said. “The Baiada company … certainly made it look that way. Once you’re inside that main building at the front, it’s like a five-star hotel.”

Australians are voracious chicken eaters, consuming an average of 55kg of chicken meat per person per year. Almost half of all meat eaten in Australia is chicken, and consumption has doubled in the past 30 years. More than 800 million chickens will be slaughtered this financial year to meet the demand.
Once fully operational, the Oakburn facility will account for almost 20% of that.

“We’re happy to see a commitment from a Sydney-based company to one of their regional hubs, to put in such a sophisticated [facility],” says Prof Stephen Walkden-Brown, the interim director of Poultry Hub Australia at the University of New England. “It’s a pretty big development, one of the most modern plants in the world.”
In a media release, Baiada said the company had “grown alongside” the Tamworth community for six decades, and the facility reflected the company’s commitment to the city.

“This is a long-term investment in Tamworth and the people who have supported Baiada for generations,” managing director Simon Camilleri says. “Our history in this region stretches back to the 1960s, when Charlie Baiada first established operations here, and this facility reflects our confidence in the future of Tamworth.”
But it did not answer questions about whether the new facility would also deliver improved animal welfare outcomes.

Jed Goodfellow, the director of policy and government relations at the Australian Alliance for Animals, said while the Baiada building may be state of the art, he believes “the welfare model behind it is anything but”.
Slowing the growth
A leading welfare issue, Goodfellow says, is the speed at which meat chickens grow.

“Chickens are still being selectively bred to grow at extraordinary speeds, with their bodies paying the price for ever greater efficiency,” he said. “Healthier, slower-growing breeds are now being used in many parts of the world, particularly Europe, with Norway, the Netherlands, and France producing higher welfare breeds at scale.”
“It may cost slightly more, but as their experience shows, the increase is not prohibitive, as European consumers increasingly opt for the healthier option.”
Melina Tensen, the senior scientific officer for farm animals at the RSPCA, said about 97% of chicken meat sold in Australia abides by the organisation’s welfare standards.

“It’s a pretty big deal to have most of industry achieving standards to go well above the legal minimum,” Tensen says. “Wherever animals are farmed for food – and they’re going to be farmed for food for a long time to come – we want to be in there making sure that animals are raised and handled and transported and slaughtered in ways we find acceptable.”

Welfare standards were updated this month to promote lower stocking density, variable light intensity in sheds – to allow chickens to choose between brighter and darker areas – and the phasing out of a slaughtering method called electrical water bath stunning. Those changes must be enacted by 1 January 2031 for businesses to keep their RSPCA certification.

At the same time, the RSPCA has released a new category of “enhanced” welfare standards, which are primarily focused on encouraging producers to rear slower-growing breeds. Most of Australia’s commercial chickens are two fast-growing breeds, the Ross 308 and the Cobb 500, which reach slaughter weight at between four and six weeks of age.

Tensen said the RSPCA would ultimately like to see chicken meat producers replace fast-growing breeds with ones associated with higher welfare standards, but consumers would have to help achieve that transition.

“The longer it takes to grow, the greater cost,” she said. “We definitely encourage consumers to be vocal about supporting this transition … because every dollar you spend is a message to the retailer.”

articles.title: AI hack of Medicare exposes Australia’s vulnerabilities and experts warn ‘there is more of this to come’
articles.summary:
Council on AI Strategy chief says incident unlikely to be isolated and country should enhance capability to detect and report incidents

  • Get our

blocks.text: Technology experts have warned revelations an artificial intelligence agent hacked Medicare’s internal systems will not be the only dangerous breach of government data and have called for Australia to boost its protections against the growing risk.

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, challenged the OpenAI boss, Sam Altman, on Thursday after the company’s agent infiltrated systems run by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, Victoria’s Department of Health, the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, and the Medicare statistics reporting service portal of Services Australia.
OpenAI alerted the government earlier this month to the June hacking via an email to a public-facing address, a situation Albanese called “obviously unacceptable”.
But the Australian Council on AI Strategy chief executive, Anna-Maria Arabia, said the case was unlikely to be an isolated incident.
“All of the evidence shows that our operating systems are vulnerable,” she told Guardian Australia.
“Frontier AI now has capability to expose those vulnerabilities at a rate quicker than we can keep up, quicker than we can patch them.

“When the companies are undertaking tests in what they think are secure environments, and when there are breaches of those environments and these incidences do happen, whether it’s accidental or not, what we’re seeing is the frontier AI capability exposing these vulnerabilities.
“All evidence suggests that there is more of this to come.”
Arabia said Australia needed to quickly enhance capability to detect and report incidents, and the country should host AI training labs here.
Johanna Weaver, Australia’s former chief cyber negotiator at the United Nations, agreed more incidents were inevitable.
Weaver is a member of the advisory board to the minister for government services, Katy Gallagher, and the executive director of the Tech Policy Design Institute.
“Cybersecurity experts have been warning that frontier models and AI agents could expose vulnerabilities in critical systems. What we are seeing now is the tip of the iceberg.
“Governments need to draw a clear line: if companies cannot control their AI systems, they should not release them publicly.”
The US Studies Centre expert Olivia Shen warned AI companies should not be allowed to decide on their own disclosure obligations for hacks and breaches.
“We just don’t know how big the problem is. It could be the tip of the iceberg, but either way, we can’t be ignoring the risk.

“It’s all happening at a time when Australia is designing our national standards on AI. It hasn’t been entirely clear if those national standards were going to be very hyper-focused on datacentres and leave governance questions as a bit of a bolt-on.
“I think this strengthens the argument that you need to have some pretty clear standards, even just based on mandatory incident reporting, built in.”

Intelligence agency the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) is reviewing how prepared the government is to block and respond to hacking by AI. Officials will look at policies around how AI companies should report cyber-incidents to the government, and how cooperative companies should be during and after an attack.
It will also investigate whether the current laws and systems are adequate to stop AI, and how government systems can be strengthened.
The shadow industry minister, Andrew Hastie, called for Australia to develop its own domestic AI capability, instead of relying on the US.
“If there’s rogue AI agents out there, we need to have our own defensive AI agents protecting Australian government data, our private sector, and other things that are important to us,” he said.
The Greens demanded Labor call in the new US ambassador, David Brat, to establish what President Donald Trump knew about the attack.

“This breach by a foreign AI company on an Australian government database is deeply alarming and brings home the risks that these out-of-control tech corporations pose,” acting leader, Mehreen Faruqi, said.
“The fact that the government did not even know it happened is disturbing.”

articles.title: Boy, 16, held in ‘cramped’ prison cell alone for 22 hours a day for weeks, Victorian ombudsman finds
articles.summary:
Ombudsman finds government breached teen’s human rights, saying the conditions ‘bordered on solitary confinement’

  • Get our

blocks.text: A 16-year-old boy was held in conditions akin to solitary confinement in adult prison for 22 hours a day, leading him to have suicidal thoughts, a Victorian ombudsman report has revealed.

The report, tabled in parliament on Thursday, found the Department of Justice and Community Safety breached the teen’s human rights when transferring him from the Parkville Youth Justice Precinct to the maximum-security Melbourne Assessment Prison in early 2025.
The teen was transferred after he attacked staff, following two formal warnings he would be moved to an adult prison if his “violent behaviour” continued.
When he arrived at the adult prison he was separated from others due to his age, with records showing he spent an average of more than 22 hours in his cell each day for six weeks.
The ombudsman, Marlo Baragwanath, said the conditions “bordered on solitary confinement”.
The report described the cell as “cramped and worn”, with the boy telling the ombudsman he couldn’t see out of the window.
“I was shocked … if you’re in some type of environment like that, I guess you have no hope,” he said. “After a while, it starts playing with your mind.”
Even during his outside hours, he was confined to what the ombudsman described as “effectively a room that is open to the sky” and handcuffed due to his history of violence.

blocks.caption: The designated outdoor area at the prison unit. Photograph: Victorian ombudsman

blocks.text: He ate his meals in his cell and drank straight from the tap, because a guard wouldn’t provide a cup.
“I was like … ‘I’m not a dog,’ you know. [The guard] was like, ‘Huh, you are, mate,’” the teen said.

He also had no in-person visits from family for the six weeks, telling the ombudsman he was told he wouldn’t be able to touch them: “If I see them, I want to touch them ‘cause, you know, that’s my family.”
The experience led him to suffer “dark, dark thoughts”.
“My cell was always dark. I can’t see anything,” he said. “It was playing with my mind. Started thinking stuff I’ve never thought before … a lot of self-harm … Suicidal stuff.”

Under Victorian law, a child aged 15 or older can be transferred to an adult prison as a last resort. However, the ombudsman found proper consideration was not given to the child’s human rights in making the transfer application.
after newsletter promotion

“I know many people will find it difficult to sympathise with a child who has been repeatedly violent towards youth justice staff. But human rights apply to everyone, including people accused or convicted of a crime,” Baragwanath said.

Tracy Beaton, Victoria’s principal commissioner at the Commission for Children and Young People, said “children’s human rights should never be an afterthought” and welcomed the ombudsman’s eight recommendations, including to ban the transfer of children into adult prisons, though it was rejected by the government.
Mindy Sotiri, the executive director of the Justice Reform Initiative, said the report was “indicative of a system that is failing”.
“Quite aside from the harm that is caused to children in these circumstances, this approach does absolutely nothing to rehabilitate that child or reduce the risk of them reoffending,” Sotiri said.

The Victorian senator Lidia Thorpe said: “Children need love and care and support. When we know that it costs over a million dollars to lock up a child, that money could be better in the wraparound services that actually make a child well.”

The Victorian Greens justice spokesperson, Katherine Copsey, described the report as an “indictment” of the Labor government, who last year introduced “adult time for violent crime” laws in response to rising youth offending.

The Victorian Liberal spokesperson for youth justice, Renee Heath, said Labor was “failing at both ends of the youth justice system” – pointing to an audit released on Wednesday that found there was no evidence the government’s $40m crime prevention program was working.
According to the ombudsman, the teen was transferred back to an adult prison after he turned 18 and was no longer separated for safety.

articles.title: Man, 105, being investigated over murders at Nazi PoW camp
articles.summary:
Centenarian accused of being accessory to multiple murders at Stalag 326 VI K in west Germany, as judiciary race to prosecute suspects before they die

A 105-year-old man is under…

blocks.text: A 105-year-old man is under investigation on suspicion of being an accessory to multiple murders at a Nazi prisoner of war camp, German prosecutors have said.
The case, which is being handled by the public prosecutor’s office in Dortmund, centres on the Stalag 326 VI K camp in western Germany, in what is now the state of North Rhine-Westphalia.

“The 105-year-old suspect is thought to have been a guard at the prisoner of war camp Stalag 326 VI K in the Senne region of western Germany,” prosecutors said in a statement. The man is “accused of being an accessory to multiple murders owing to his activities there”, they said.
The Senne camp housed between 180,000 and 200,000 Soviet prisoners of war between 1941 and April 1945, when it was liberated by American troops.

The investigation is the result of an urgent last-minute scramble by the judiciary to prosecute alleged participants in the Nazi killing machine before they die. The judicial efforts stem in part from a recognition that many of the suspects who have escaped prosecution in the eight decades since the end of the second world war on the grounds that they were considered to have played an insignificant role were in fact integral to the implementation of the Hitler regime’s murderous aims.

A judicial precedent was set by the court case of John Demjanjuk, a former guard at the Nazi Sobibór death camp in occupied Poland, who was convicted in 2011 of being an accomplice to the murders of more than 28,000 Jews that took place in the time he worked there.

Prosecutors had sought Ukraine-born Demjanjuk’s extradition from his Ohio home to Germany for years, arguing that he was complicit in the crimes committed at Sobibór despite a lack of evidence that he had directly killed anyone.
Demjanjuk died aged 91 in March 2012 awaiting an appeal due to his age and frailty, which meant he did not go to prison.

blocks.caption: John Demjanjuk, a former guard at the Sobibór death camp, died without going to prison. Photograph: David Rubinger/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Demjanjuk case lowered the bar for proof of complicity, paving the way for other nonagenarians and more recently centenarians to stand trial.

The most prominent trial of recent years, and representative of what Hannah Arendt, a political theorist, described as a Schreibtischtäter (desk perpetrator, or bureaucratic mediator), was that of Irmgard Furchner, who worked at the Stutthof concentration camp between 1943 and 1945 as a secretary to the camp commandant. She was given a two-year suspended sentence for her role as an accessory to murder.
Her trial was, contrary to normal rules, filmed for historical purposes. Furchner made headlines after running away from her retirement home on the scheduled opening day of her trial.

Josef Schütz, a former guard at the Sachsenhausen concentration camp north of Berlin, was sentenced for being an accomplice to murder to five years in prison in June 2022. He died the following year, aged 102.
In April last year an alleged former guard at Sachsenhausen died before he was able to face trial over charges of complicity in the murder of more than 3,300 people.

A separate investigation was opened last year by Dortmund prosecutors into a 100-year-old former guard at a PoW camp in Hemer, North Rhine-Westphalia, which also held mainly Soviet prisoners. He is suspected of participating in executions of prisoners between December 1943 and September 1944.

The new investigation was initiated by the Central Office for the Investigation of National Socialist Crimes in Ludwigsburg, in the southern state of Baden-Württemberg, which passed its preliminary investigation into the man to public prosecutors along with that of another former guard. The other suspect has since died, according to German media.

If the trial goes ahead, like other recent cases it is expected to throw light on the Stalag system in general and on Senne in particular, drawing survivors and historians to give evidence. Up to 5.7 million Soviet prisoners were held captivity in Germany. More than half did not survive.
