articles.title: Ex-ConCom member backs exclusion of detained senators from impeachment vote threshold
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court committed no constitutional violation in basing Vice President Sara Duterte"s conviction threshold on participating senators, a 1987 Constitution framer said.

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 6:37pm
The Senate impeachment court committed no constitutional violation in basing Vice President Sara Duterte’s conviction threshold on participating senators, a 1987 Constitution framer said.
“Yes, I think it's correct,” Christian Monsod, a member of the Constitutional Commission, told Super Radyo dzBB when asked if the impeachment did not violate any law with their ruling.

“During the constitutional commission, we could not foresee everything that would happen in the country. Nagkaroon ng plunder law, the plunder law said that those who are accused and detained, they suspended the power of those government officers,” said Monsod. “So suspended lahat ng kanilang power. So they are senators only in name, but no longer in substance. Kaya dapat hindi sila kasali sa denominator.”

(During the constitutional commission, we could not foresee everything that would happen in the country. A plunder law was enacted, and the plunder law stated that those accused and detained would have their powers as government officers suspended,” Monsod said. “So all of their power is suspended. They are senators only in name, but no longer in substance. That’s why they shouldn't be included in the denominator.)

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday voted to base the two-thirds vote to convict the impeached Vice President Sara Duterte on the number of senators who are capable of "legally and factually participating in the impeachment proceedings."

The vote, in effect, set aside the ruling on July 6 by presiding officer Senator-judge Francis "Chiz" Escudero, who set the number of votes needed to convict at 16, or two-thirds of all the 24 senators.

Thirteen senator-judges voted in favor of the motion put forward by Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo, who sought reconsideration of the July 6 ruling after some senators became unavailable to participate in the impeachment trial.
“So the two-thirds ratio, that is unchangeable. But the denominator, it turns out, may be changeable and we did not foresee that this shall occur with the plunder law,” Monsod said.
“Kung fixed yung 16, we would have put it there?” he added.
“Our guideline was the 1935 Constitution. So ang amin lang pong binago ay yung three-fourths to two-thirds; we left it alone,” he also said.
The latest ruling by the Senate impeachment court would mean that the four absent senators won’t be allowed to participate in the voting even via teleconferencing.
Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained on plunder and other related charges due to their alleged involvement in flood control and undeclared campaign donations, respectively.
For his part, Monsod said that the senators who are charged with crimes shouldn’t be included in the count.
“They committed a crime. Therefore, they lost their powers as senators by committing a crime. So they should not be included in the counting of the denominator,” he said.
Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, meanwhile, remains at large amid a warrant of arrest from the International Criminal Court in connection with the previous administration's bloody drug war.
Senator Loren Legarda recently extended her medical leave abroad due to a lung condition.
In Legarda’s case, Monsod said that her presence in the deliberations must be taken into consideration.
“Yung Loren, we will see what happens and why she is absent. Because she participated in the deliberations before she left for that leave,” he said. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: [Pastilan] The Davao lies are having a meeting
articles.summary: The most hilarious idea, of course, is that everybody is telling the truth simultaneously

blocks.text: The most hilarious idea, of course, is that everybody is telling the truth simultaneously

items: The Gencorp affair has escalated into a political scandal involving Vice President Sara Duterte, whose declared business interest in Gencorp contradicts corporate records that do not list her as an owner.

Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte confirmed contracts worth over P30 million awarded to Gencorp, yet claimed ignorance of his sister's connection to the company, raising questions about governance and accountability.
Removing Sara Duterte from office would have implications on political funding, as donors may reconsider their investments in a candidate facing disqualification.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
There is a special stage in a political scandal when the facts stop cooperating with the explanations.
This is usually when the explanations begin multiplying and clashing with each other. The Gencorp affair has reached that stage.
According to Vice President Sara Duterte’s own Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), she has/had a business interest in Gencorp.

blocks.caption: How Sara Duterte-linked company got millions in Davao City Hall contracts

blocks.text: Then came the clarification that Gencorp is not her company, based on documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

This is an intriguing distinction. Apparently, one can have a declared business interest in a company without actually having an interest in the company. The dictionary may eventually need to be called as a hostile witness.

But then the contracts arrived, and Davao City’s government gave Gencorp contracts worth over P30 million starting in 2022, according to Mayor Baste Duterte, Sara’s younger brother. That is considerably more than the P14 million initially reported. That’s a hell of a lot of spaghetti, burgers, ketchup and whatever else comes with a side of indigestion.

In a statement, Baste swears he knew nothing about his sister’s connection to Gencorp. He also pointed to corporate filings with the SEC showing that the vice president’s name does not appear as an incorporator, director or stockholder.
And there, suddenly, is the problem.

If the corporate records say one thing and the vice president’s SALN says another, someone is eventually going to have to explain what Sara Duterte meant by declaring an interest in Gencorp, and why that interest does not appear in the company’s corporate records.

So Sara Duterte declared an interest, but Gencorp’s corporate records do not identify her as an owner. Her brother confirms that the city government awarded Gencorp contracts, but quickly does a Pontius Pilate by adding that neither he nor other city hall officials knew about his sister’s declared interest in the firm.
The most hilarious idea, of course, is that everybody is telling the truth simultaneously. In effect, Sara’s interest exists somewhere other than where one would normally expect to find it.

The prospect of the tough-talking Baste Duterte taking the witness stand in the impeachment court ought to be entertaining, if only because his confirmation of the contracts has handed prosecutors precisely the factual record they wanted, while his attempt to distance himself from his sister’s connection to Gencorp has raised rather more questions than it has answered.

Baste should sack whoever advised him to make that statement, and then ask whoever drafted it whether they have ever encountered the rudimentary concept of self-preservation. He may have imagined he was closing the door, but instead he seems to have flung open the gates.

If a city mayor can preside over millions of pesos in contracts involving a company in which his own sister has declared a business interest, and then plead ignorance of the entire arrangement, the question is no longer merely whether the contracts were properly procured. It is whether a mayor who knows so little about the business of his own government is actually governing it at all, or merely occupying the chair while the paperwork conducts the city in his place.

As the prosecutors have correctly pointed out, this is where “due diligence” enters the room, looking as though it has just discovered that it was invited to the wrong party. Nobody expects a mayor to know everything, of course. But he is surely expected to know enough about the machinery of his own government to account for millions in public contracts.

“I didn’t know” is not a defense so much as an admission that makes the question unavoidable. If a mayor can invoke ignorance of millions in government contracts as his excuse, one is entitled to wonder whether Davao elected a mayor or merely paid for a nameplate.
And the more this Gencorp story is examined, the stranger the central contradiction becomes.
At some point, the question ceases to be whether there are too many contradictions. The question is why there are so many.
Political scandals often begin with one inconvenient fact. They become crises when every attempt to explain that fact produces another inconvenient fact.
Gencorp is beginning to resemble less a company than a group project in which nobody remembers who wrote what.
And the lies, if that is what they are, appear to have scheduled another meeting.

Meanwhile, the impeachment court has voted to make the two-thirds threshold for conviction contingent on the actual roll call when judgment day arrives. Simply put, the once near-fantastical prospect of removing Sara Duterte from office and barring her from holding public office has become a live possibility.
What is less discussed is what this does to the flow of money.

It is difficult to imagine that the 2028 presidential race is not already being plotted, financed and, somewhere in the shadows, quietly bankrolled. But political money is rarely charitable. It likes a plausible return on investment.
Would a political funder keep releasing millions into a campaign whose principal could soon be removed from office and disqualified from seeking public office?
Come on. Political donors may be many things, but sentimental is rarely one of them. Pastilan.– Rappler.com

articles.title: Indian oil and gas heir made professor of sustainability at Newcastle University
articles.summary:
Incredulity over role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo

Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the…

blocks.text: Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.

The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.

Ambani is the son of India’s richest person, Mukesh Ambani, who made his fortune primarily in oil and gas, owns the world’s largest oil refinery and has close ties with the ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP). Mukesh Ambani has enthusiastically praised BJP policies, and firms linked to his Reliance conglomerate have recently made significant donations to the party. The prime minister, Narendra Modi, attended Anant Ambani’s lavish 2024 wedding in Mumbai.

Anant Amabani, 31, who is leads on renewable energy on the Reliance Group’s executive board and is worth an estimated £90bn, has set up Vantara, a 1,400-hectare (3,500-acre) private zoo near the family’s oil refining facilities in Gujarat, which reportedly has more than 150,000 animals including 200 lions, 250 leopards and 900 crocodiles, and where he hosted his opulent pre-wedding celebrations attended by celebrity guests and politicians.
Conservation groups have previously raised questions about how some of the animals were sourced, given many were endangered species. Vantara has never been found guilty of any wrongdoing.

blocks.caption: The Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, visiting the Vantara zoo in Gujarat in March 2025. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: The university’s announcement was met with incredulity and derision from academic staff and Indian and international conservationists and environmentalists.

Ramachandra Guha, a leading Indian public intellectual and the author of the book Speaking With Nature: The Origins of Indian Environmentalism, said: “I must say that it is a rather mystifying choice. As a scholar of Indian and global environmentalism, I can name at least 50 – perhaps 100 – individuals who are far better qualified to be thus honoured. They include soil scientists, energy scientists, water conservation experts, community forest workers, ecologists, pollution abatement experts etc who have made real and tangible contributions to a more sustainable future for India and Indians.

“I wonder on whose advice Newcastle University has acted, and whether it did due diligence on what has and has not been done in these fields. Its appointment of Mr Ambani is puzzling in the extreme, and is likely to adversely affect the university’s institutional credibility and intellectual standing.”

blocks.caption: A Newcastle University spokesperson said the professorship ‘recognises Mr Ambani’s contributions to conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship’. Photograph: Washington Imaging/Alamy

blocks.text: Bhuvan Mangalore, an Indian investigator into illegal wildlife trade who is completing a dissertation on Vantara at Anglia Ruskin University, asked: “Is this a joke?”
Prof Matt Perry, the chair of the University and College Union branch at Newcastle University, said staff members had objected to the appointment citing environmental concerns.

Prof Lyla Mehta, the head of the climate, environment and sustainability department at the University of Sussex’s Institute of Development Studies, shared concerns that “as public funding for universities falls, there is a real danger that billionaire and corporate money begins to shape academia”.
She said: “Universities are supposed to be places that question power and hold corporations to account, not give them academic legitimacy.”
In April, Anant Ambani launched Vantara University, billed as the world’s first global university dedicated to wildlife conservation and veterinary science.

Lorne Stockman, a research co-director at Oil Change International, said: “At a time when the climate crisis demands an urgent phaseout of oil and gas, we must demand our publicly funded institutions do better.”
after newsletter promotion

In 2025, an investigation by the German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung found that many animals delivered to Vantara arrived through countries with opaque wildlife trading networks such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the United Arab Emirates, raising concerns that endangered species may have been illegally trafficked.

In August last year, an investigation by India’s supreme court, which lasted less than three weeks, cleared the zoo’s operators of any wrongdoing. A subsequent fact-finding mission into the zoo by Cites, the UN body that regulates the trade of endangered species, found that some of the permits used to bring animals to Vantara were probably forged.
Its report said: “There is a need for caution to ensure that imports of large numbers of animals by these facilities are not inadvertently creating a demand for illegally sourced animals.”

Cites recommended restrictions on India’s imports of endangered wild animals. However, it subsequently reversed its decision after objections from India, the US and Japan at a Cites meeting after they argued there was not enough proof of illegal imports.
In August, the zoo launched a “reset” in its operations by appointing a former Cites head to oversee its operations and said it would voluntarily pause all wildlife imports until June next year.

blocks.caption: An employee watching news related to Vantara on a website at his office in Bengaluru.  Photograph: Idrees Mohammed/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Vantara has declined to comment. The Ambani family and Vantara have previously denied the allegations of wildlife trafficking. They have said: “Our mission and focus continues to be the rescue, rehabilitation and care of animals.”

A Newcastle University spokesperson said: “The award of a professorship of practice recognises Mr Ambani’s contributions to conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship through his work with Vantara, a wildlife rescue and conservation initiative, and as the executive lead for the Reliance Group’s transition toward a green energy future.”

articles.title: A pub trip with another man: court views CCTV footage of Jesse Baird found on Beau Lamarre-Condon’s devices
articles.summary: Former NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies before concealing bodies in bags bought from sports store

blocks.text: Beau Lamarre-Condon was seen sizing up a surfboard bag used to dispose of a victim days before the police officer murdered two men, prosectors have alleged in a Sydney court, with chilling CCTV footage shown to the jury.
Months earlier, the 31-year-old had asked a friend over a video call to help him obtain something, and then formed a gun gesture with his hand, the NSW supreme court trial heard on Thursday.
Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, with his police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
The 31-year-old earlier this week pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
CCTV footage taken from Miranda Westfield on 17 February was played to the NSW supreme court trial on Thursday showing Lamarre-Condon’s movements before the alleged murders.
In the compilation, Lamarre-Condon’s grey Tesla is seen passing by the shopping centre before the police officer and a friend enter a Decathlon store.
The pair walk straight to the surfboard bag section, where Lamarre-Condon runs his hands across the options before picking out a cover.
He holds it up and appears to measure it against his friend’s height as the other man stands straight. The bag clears his friend’s head by a few centimetres.
Watching from the pews of the Sydney courtroom, Davies and Baird’s family shook their heads as the footage was played.
During the prosecution’s openings on Monday, crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC alleged Lamarre-Condon asked his friend whether he would fit in the bag.
In the footage, Lamarre-Condon takes the bag to the cashier and pays for it using $90 in cash, according to receipts shown to the court.
Two days later, the police officer would allegedly shoot the two men and place Baird in the bag bought from the Westfield, the prosecution alleged.
Lamarre-Condon returned to the same store shortly after the shooting to buy a second surfboard bag to conceal Davies’ body, Hatfield said.
More than 14,000 hours of CCTV footage was obtained from 200 locations during the police investigation, the detective in charge, Sasha Pinazza, told the court.

Other videos played to the jury on Thursday showed Lamarre-Condon collecting the alleged murder weapon from a police gun locker the day before the shootings, and his mother at a car rental business picking up the vehicle he would use to drive to Baird’s house.

blocks.caption: A police photograph of the gun allegedly used in the shootings. Photograph: Supplied by NSW supreme court

blocks.text: In footage from the morning of the alleged crime, the police man is seen walking in the vicinity of Baird’s home before CCTV from a neighbouring house captures the sound of three gunshots.
after newsletter promotion
The audio had been played during the crown’s opening remarks on Monday. But as the recording was again heard in the court room, the couple’s friends and family flinched at the sounds of the bangs.
The prosecution has told the jury that Lamarre-Condon developed an “infatuation and obsession” with Baird that manifested in compulsive behaviour during their brief relationship.

During his opening statement, Hatfield said Lamarre-Condon had misused his authority as a police officer after CCTV footage of Baird with another man at the Royal hotel in Paddington in May 2023 was allegedly found on Lamarre-Condon’s personal devices.
His behaviour allegedly escalated after the younger man broke things off for the last time in November 2023.

blocks.caption: Luke Davies (left) and Jesse Baird. Composite: Supplied by the NSW supreme court

blocks.text: An old friend of Lamarre-Condon, who used the pseudonym Alex Carrol in court, told the jury the accused called her on 23 November 2023.
They began a call before Lamarre-Condon said: “Can I ask you for something? But I can’t ask you over the phone – can we FaceTime?”
He then asked for a favour from the father of her children, referred to in court as Robert Thomas.
Carrol told the court Lamarre-Condon formed his hand into a gun and mouthed the words “can Robert get me a gun?”

She and her sister, who could see the screen, looked at each other in shock. Carrol then asked Lamarre-Condon: “Why would you ask for a gun, you’re in the police?” He shrugged off the question, the court heard.
It’s alleged Lamarre-Condon began planning to murder Baird in early 2024.
The defence team has claimed the police officer was acting in self-defence after he disguised himself as an Uber Eats driver and entered Baird’s home on the day of the shootings.
The trial before justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: Win Gatchalian: Threshold vote does not indicate Sara Duterte impeachment outcome
articles.summary: The decision of senator-judges to effectively overturn the earlier ruling on the prescribed number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte does not indicate what the outcome of the…

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 6:21pm

The decision of senator-judges to effectively overturn the earlier ruling on the prescribed number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte does not indicate what the outcome of the impeachment trial will be, Senate President Win Gatchalian on Thursday.
Thirteen senator-judges voted to base the two-thirds conviction vote requirement on the number of senators who participated in the impeachment proceedings.

This overturned the July 6 ruling by presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero, which recognized the base number as relating to the full 24-member Senate, thus setting the conviction requirement at 16.
Gatchalian disagreed that the 13 who voted in favor of the revised base number will eventually vote to convict Duterte.

"Malayo 'yun. Depende pa rin 'yan sa presentation ng evidence. Depende pa rin 'yan kung anong sasabihin ng mga testigo. So, hindi pa 'yan 'yung boto para i-convict o hindi pa rin 'yan 'yung boto para i-acquit," Gatchalian said in an ambush interview when asked about the matter.
(Far from it. It still depends on the presentation of the evidence. It depends on what the witnesses will say. So, those are not the votes to convict, and those are not the votes to acquit.)
Gatchalian added that this decision from the court was also not binding to future impeachment trials either.

The Senate president was also asked if the latest decision made things more complicated for the impeachment court since, hypothetically, an absentee senator could also show up suddenly on the voting day without participating in the trial.

"Hindi naman siya complicated dahil ang basic doon, kung present ka, puwede kang bumoto. So that is the basic. At 'yan 'yun ang pinaka-fair. Dahil kung hindi ka magiging present, automatic, acquit ka na kaagad,” Gatchalian said.
(It is not complicated because it is basic, if you are present, you can vote. So that is the basics. And that is what is most fair. Because if you are not present, automatically, you vote acquit.)
In case an absentee senator-judge did show up however, Gatchalian said he would assume that they read the transcript or followed the trial on YouTube.
There are currently two senators who are detained over plunder charges. Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are imprisoned at the Quezon City Jail.

Meanwhile, Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa has not been seen in public following the International Criminal Court's issuance of an arrest warrant against him. Senator Loren Legarda is on extended medical leave in France.
For example, Gatchalian said, if Dela Rosa was to show up somehow on voting day, then he could still vote.
On the other hand, even if a senator-judge attended every day of the trial, if they were absent on voting day, they would not be able to vote. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Poland says Starlink station fire 'act of sabotage'
articles.summary: Polish Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said Warsaw believed the attack aimed to disrupt internet access for the Ukrainian military, calling it "an element of the next phase of hybrid…

image.caption: Starlink stations in Poland help service UkraineImage: NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Warsaw considers a fire that broke out at a Starlink station in central Poland to be an act of sabotage, Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said on Thursday.

"This act of sabotage was deliberately designed to disable the station ... disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army," Gawkowski, who also serves as digital minister, told public broadcaster TVP.
He said the fire at the station belonging to Polish state-owned telecom company Exatel broke out late on Wednesday.
"There is much to suggest that we are dealing with an element of the next phase of hybrid warfare," he said.
The deputy premier said that the station was used to transmit internet traffic through Poland, including to neighboring Ukraine.
He also said there were "many indications" suggesting the incident "fits into this new Russian doctrine of attack."

blocks.caption: Gawkowski warned that the incident could reflect a 'new Russian doctrine of attack'Image: Klaudia Radecka/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Poland accuses Russia of 'hybrid' warfare

Poland and other EU and NATO member states have accused Russia of engaging in hybrid warfare, including acts of sabotage, against Ukraine's allies, since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Lying on the EU and NATO's eastern flank, Poland borders Ukraine, the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad and Moscow ally Belarus. It is one of Kyiv's strongest supporters in Europe.
Warsaw also joined the new "Carpathian Eight" regional summit launched by Ukraine last Friday.
Earlier in September, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that Russia plans to carry out "hybrid" drone and missile strikes against Ukraine's allies.
Late last year, Poland accused Russia of carrying out "state terrorism" over an act of sabotage on the Polish rail network.

articles.title: Global release announced for acclaimed Gaza documentary NAZA
articles.summary:
Theatrical rollout across 56 territories planned for documentary about Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza before film will stream on Guardian website

NAZA, the award-winning…

blocks.text: NAZA, the award-winning documentary from Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is set to be released in cinemas in more than 50 countries before a digital global release on theguardian.com.

The film, which the Guardian produced, premiered at the Venice film festival earlier this month, where it was met with a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. The documentary went on to win the special jury prize.

After screenings in Bologna and at the San Sebastián film festival, the film will receive its North American premiere on Saturday at the New York film festival before opening four days later at the IFC Center in New York City. On 9 October it will expand to Los Angeles and other key US cities before a national rollout.

A theatrical release in partnership with MK2 Films is also planned in 55 other territories, including the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Canada, Hong Kong, Brazil, Turkey, Thailand, France, Spain, Germany, Turkey, Central America and the Middle East.
After its run in cinemas, the film will stream on the Guardian’s website, for free, as part of the news organisation’s commitment to the dissemination of independent journalism.

“NAZA is grounded in rigorous journalism published over the past three years,” said Harry Davies, a Guardian investigations correspondent and one of NAZA’s producers. “But it is also a powerful piece of cinema that will soon be available on screens, large and small, around the world.”

blocks.caption: Documentary NAZA gets 25-minute standing ovation at Venice film festival premiere – video

blocks.text: A number of distributors and cinemas in Israel have been offered the film, and the Guardian is exploring ways by which NAZA can be seen in the occupied Palestinian territories.

The documentary reveals the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza. NAZA is a military acronym euphemistically used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that it expects will be killed in an airstrike.

Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film features interviews with 24 members of Israeli intelligence and military, granted on the condition of anonymity. The film builds on journalism first published by the Guardian, +972 Magazine, an Israeli-Palestinian publication, and Hebrew-language outlet Local Call between 2023 and 2025.

In 2024, Abraham and Szor won the best documentary Oscar for No Other Land, along with their two Palestinian co-directors, Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal. Jonathan Glazer, the Oscar-winning film-maker of The Zone of Interest and Under the Skin, has executive produced, while his longtime collaborator, James Wilson of JW Films, also produced the film.

The film won unanimously positive reviews at its premiere, but last week Benjamin Netanyahu and a number of senior military and far-right political figures called for the directors’ citizenship to be revoked, and accused them of “treason against the state”.

The Israeli prime minister said he would seek new laws allowing the country to strip citizenship from people who “smear” Israeli soldiers and “defame” the state of Israel. Alongside the announcement, dozens of rightwing activists gathered outside Szor’s parents’ home.
Police and border police officers were deployed at the scene. One protester called for the “death penalty for traitors” and demanded that the homes of the film-makers’ families be demolished.

Speaking on Thursday, Abraham and Szor said: “We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israelis to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible.

“The threats from the Israeli government to revoke our citizenship and the death threats do not change that and will not stop the film. We thank our colleagues for the solidarity and look forward to sharing NAZA all over the world very soon.”

Last week, 43 local human rights organisations issued a joint statement urging Israeli authorities to stop what they described as incitement and threats against the film-makers, and not to prosecute either them or their sources.
More than 1,500 Israeli film-makers have also signed a petition defending “freedom of expression and creation” and expressing solidarity with Szor and Abraham.

Their sentiments have been echoed by a number of leading film-makers around the world, including Ken Loach, Joshua Oppenheimer, Paul Laverty, Laura Poitras, Nan Goldin, Richard Eyre and Hanif Kureishi. Oppenheimer, the US director of Oscar-nominated documentaries The Act of Killing and The Look of Silence, said, “The Israeli government is waging a full-scale intimidation campaign against film directors. I am appalled and enraged.”

articles.title: [Rappler Investigates] Mystery in Sara’s SALNs
articles.summary: It's getting more interesting, isn’t it, especially from the conflict-of-interest lens?

blocks.text: How do you explain it? A company was declared and sworn to in the Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs) of Vice President Sara Duterte. But it’s nowhere to be found in documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), as multimedia reporter Patrick Cruz first discovered ahead of proceedings at the impeachment trial. (READ: Sara Duterte’s company won millions’ worth of contracts from Davao City Hall)

Next obvious question is: does the VP have a business interest in Gencorp Industries Inc., the company that figures in these contracts? Further, did she violate the Constitution, which explicitly prohibits the president, vice president, members of the Cabinet, and their deputies or assistants from having any “conflict of interest in the conduct of their office.”

Article VII of the 1987 charter bans the Vice President from participation in “any business” or being “financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the government…”

It’s as clear as day that, as Patrick found out, Gencorp obtained over P15 million in contracts from Davao City Hall when the VP’s brother, Baste Duterte, was sitting as mayor, and Sara was already elected vice president.

The SEC’s Gerardo del Rosario, company registration and monitoring director, ventured possible explanations for the discrepancy between Sara’s SALN and SEC documents pertaining to Gencorp. Read about them here.

It would be natural to surmise or speculate on possible dummy arrangements or even private trust agreements. Documents also reveal that the JTC Group of Companies is a major shareholder (almost 55%) in Gencorp. And JTC’s president is a Duterte associate, Jaime Tan Cruz, whose initials appear to correspond with the company’s name.

More digging exposed past links between Cruz and former president Rodrigo Duterte (among others, he was appointed special envoy to China, in charge of trade and investments). Tan was found to also be an incorporator of at least seven companies, some of them also appearing in the Vice President’s SALNs, identifying herself as “incorporator/stockholder” in some of these.

Getting more interesting, isn’t it, especially from the conflict-of-interest lens? The defense is expected to find ways of disentangling the Vice President from these when their turn comes. They will most likely point to the SEC documents and the absence of Sara Duterte’s names in them as proof of her non-association with these business entities.

A statement from Baste Duterte, however, disclosed that Gencorp got 19 contracts from Davao City Hall worth P33.6 million (even more than what we had initially seen). He never knew that his sister had any business interests in Gencorp, he said — but whatever happened to due diligence?

More clarity should come in the next few days when Baste appears before the impeachment trial court. If you’d like to catch up on stories related to the VP’s business interests, be sure to read the following:

Why Sara Duterte skips questions related to her impeachment

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 5:26pm

The proposed measure seeking to postpone the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) and allow five-year terms for barangay officials has been transmitted to Malacañang, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said Thursday.

"Pinadala na namin kay Presidente at sa pagkaalam po wala namang balita na ive-veto niya. So, ma-extend ng five years. Ma-extend ng additional two years 'yung incumbent na barangay official," Gatchalian told reporters.

(We already sent it to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and from what I know, there are no news that he will veto it. So, the terms of barangay officials will be extended to five years. Terms of incumbent barangay officials will be extended by two more years.)
"Wala naman akong nababalitaan na ive-veto nila ng Malacañnang, so masa-sign 'yun anytime, maybe this week," he added.
(I did not receive any news that Malacañang will veto it, so it may be signed anytime. Maybe this week.)
Gatchalian shared that the proposed measure was transmitted Wednesday, but Malacañang has yet to notify when will the President will sign it.
The BSKE is scheduled for November 2, while the filling of certificates of candidacy will be from September 28 to October 5, 2026.
Last week, the Senate approved on third and final reading a bill seeking to extend the term of office of barangay officials and SK members to five years instead of four.
With 13 affirmative votes, five negative votes, and no abstentions, the upper chamber approved Senate Bill 2387 during its plenary session.

The measure seeks to amend Republic Act 12232 by revising the current four-year term of barangay and SK officials to five years, and moving the next BSKE from the first to the second Monday of November 2028.

It also provides that no elective barangay official shall serve for more than two consecutive terms in the same position, while no elective SK official shall serve for more than one term in the same position.

Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero, the measure's principal author and sponsor, said the five-year term would give barangay and SK officials more time to plan, implement, and evaluate programs before the next elections. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Opportunities abound as Philippines to become aged society by 2028 -- CPD
articles.summary: The Philippines will be classified as an “aged society” by 2028, which will be accompanied by more potential opportunities for the country's development, the Commission on Population and Development…

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 5:02pm

The Philippines will be classified as an “aged society” by 2028, which will be accompanied by more potential opportunities for the country's development, the Commission on Population and Development (CPD) said Thursday.

Speaking at the 2026 World Contraception Day Forum in Pasig City, CPD Deputy Executive Director III Lolito Tacardon said the proportion of the working age population is steadily outpacing the non-working population.
As of 2024, 66.2% of the country's population was 15 to 65 years old, which is considered to be the working age group.
Meanwhile, Filipinos aged 0 to 14 years old are at 27.7% of the population, and those aged 65 and above were at 6.1%. The latter two age groups are the non-working population.

"And 6.1% of our older populations, we are getting close to the estimated period where the Philippines will be experiencing or be will considered as an aged society by 2028, because by UN (United Nations) definition, a country is considered to be an aging society if the proportion of its 65 years old and above, is at 7% already," Tacardon said in a mix of English and Filipino.

Tacardon said that 16 out of the 18 regions in the Philippines experienced slower population growth rates—with Bicol even having a negative population growth rate. The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is the only region with an increasing population growth rate.
Window for development

According to Tacardon, there is a "time-bound opportunity" for the Philippines to use this period to advance socioeconomic development. The large working age population could help develop the country.

If the government is able to provide more employment opportunities, the working population could have better income and savings, Tacardon said. This older population could then still contribute to the economy later.

"This period is very tight because… by around 2050, 'yung working age population natin will start to decrease na rin, and ang tataas ay 'yung portion of older population naman," Tacardon said, citing data from the Philippine Statistics Authority.
(This period is very tight because… by around 2050, our working age population will also decrease and then the portion of the older population will increase.)
Quality of life

Tacardon said this is a good opportunity for people to focus more on improving the quality of their lives. For example, if a household already believed that they have enough children, they could invest in other opportunities such as education.

While family planning was initially used to control population growth, it is now a chance to help prepare people for having children. Tacardon said family planning still allowed people control over their reproductive right.

"Women have to make choices between having children and being part of the labor force. Hindi sila makapag-participate sa labor force kasi mayroon silang anak to take care of. Pero hindi ba puwede pagsabayin?" Tacardon said.

(Women have to make choices between having children and being part of the labor force. They could not participate in the labor force because they have a child to take care of. But can this not happen at the same time?)
"Family planning… regardless of their conditions, they should achieve their personal aspiration," Tacardon said in a mix of English and Filipino. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Judge blocks Trump's White House media ban, orders access to be restored
articles.summary: A federal judge temporarily blocked U.S. President Donald Trump's move to ban three news outlets from the White House grounds, saying early Thursday that CNN, MS NOW and Politico must have their…

image.caption: President Donald Trump speaks to reporters as he arrives at the White House on Marine One, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026, in Washington, after greeting China's President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews. (Manuel Balce Ceneta/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

A federal judge temporarily blocked U.S. President Donald Trump's move to ban three news outlets from the White House grounds, saying early Thursday that CNN, MS NOW and Politico must have their access restored.
The legal battle has unfolded just weeks ‌before the November 3 midterm elections

It's the latest development in an escalating showdown between Trump and media outlets whose coverage he dislikes. Trump announced he was banning the outlets Friday, assailing what he called "fake news," and later arguing that their reporting was a risk to national security. The outlets argued they were singled out because of the content of their coverage, calling ban a blatant First Amendment violation.

In an order, U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly said the media outlets had met the legal thresholds to obtain a temporary restraining order, in effect for 14 days. He said they were likely to succeed in showing that their White House press passes were revoked without due process.

items: MS NOW, CNN and Politico sue Trump administration over White House ban

blocks.text: "This is a high bar, but Plaintiffs have met it," he wrote.

Kelly said the government must have clear standards for conduct that would lead to revoking a press pass. He called the standard of objectionable reporting outlined in letters that the White House sent the outlets days after banning their reporters "so vague it hardly does the trick."
Kelly — whom Trump nominated in 2017 and who ordered a CNN journalist's access restored in a similar case in 2018 — heard arguments Wednesday and ended the hearing without ruling.
Temporary restraining orders are typically designed to preserve the status quo pending a closer review of the case by the court.

"This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law," Theodore Boutrous Jr., attorney for the outlets, said in an emailed statement. "We greatly appreciate the court's swift action."
3 U.S. media outlets sue Trump administration
The White House did not immediately respond to an email from The Associated Press requesting comment.

In an emergency hearing Wednesday, Kelly said his decision must be guided by prior rulings in comparable First Amendment cases, even if the government disagrees with them. His decision noted that the White House argued that previous cases cited had been wrongly decided.
"Maybe," Kelly wrote, "but this Court is bound by D.C. Circuit precedent, full stop."

Kelly also rejected the White House's claim that revoking the press passes was necessary for national security, saying officials did little to back up that notion. "Nothing in the record... suggests that the revocation of Plaintiffs' hard passes was motivated by national security concerns," he wrote.
"The Court is skeptical ... that Defendants' interest in safeguarding national security is the actual motivation for, or is even advanced by, the revocation of Plaintiffs' hard passes."
Did Trump just silence himself? | About That
In arguments Wednesday, attorneys debated access to White House and any risk to national security

Boutrous argued about the urgent need for a change, saying there had been irreparable harm to the outlets at a time of momentous news events. "We're at war. We have world leaders coming to Washington."
Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik had reiterated the administration's point that the president had the right to choose who gets into the White House.
"Access to the White House is a privilege, not a right," Velchik said.

In arguing that Trump was not engaging in viewpoint discrimination, Velchik said the president had criticized other news organizations even more harshly -- such as calling ABC "the worst" -- but hadn't banned them.
"The president should be able to take immediate action to protect national security," Velchik told the court.
In response, Boutrous said, "Suddenly it's a national security case," arguing that the president brought up that point only after the lawsuit was filed.
Trump "keeps proving our point," Boutrous said, describing how the president has consistently used negative coverage of him as justification for the ban.

articles.title: Morocco: Center-right PAM leads in parliamentary election
articles.summary: PAM is part of Morocco's outgoing ruling coalition and was founded by an adviser to the king. The moderate Islamist Justice and Development Party surged amid increasing voter apathy.

image.caption: The PAM party gained 10 seats, according to provisional results, while its two coalition partners suffered lossesImage: Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP

blocks.text: Morocco's center-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) took first place in Wednesday's parliamentary election, according to provisional results.
PAM is part of Morocco's outgoing ruling coalition.
The party won 97 out of 395 seats in parliament, 10 seats more than in 2021.
It was founded in 2008 by an adviser to the king and advocates social modernization and moderate secularist views. It is largely seen as close to the Moroccan monarchy.
The next coalition government will oversee preparations for the 2030 World Cup.

The vote is not expected to fundamentally alter the balance of power in the North African kingdom. As the country is a semi-constitutional monarchy, Morocco's King Mohammed VI retains substantial powers in both policy direction and foreign affairs.
How did other parties fare in Morocco's election?
The National Rally of Independents (RNI), the senior partner in the outgoing coalition, dropped from 102 to 66 seats, putting it at second place.
The smallest member of the governing coalition, the right-wing Istiqlal party also saw losses, taking 65 seats, 16 fewer than in 2021.
The moderate Islamist opposition Justice and Development Party surged to 54 seats, compared to just 13 in 2021.
Moroccans head to the polls amid rising voter apathy
Election marked by increasing voter apathy
The election saw turnout of 38%, marking the lowest level since 2007. Nearly 16 million people were registered to vote.
Only around 4% of registered voters were aged 18 to 24.
In 2025, Morocco was rocked by Gen Z-led protests, which were the largest in the country since the Arab Spring in the early 2010s.
Mistrust in politicians and issues regarding living conditions were widely blamed for the low turnout.
"I'm not going to vote because I have lost all faith in the political class," 50-year-old Majda Bakatir told the AFP news agency.
"We want our country to move forward, but politicians do not seem to care about our problems regarding healthcare, education, and purchasing power," she said.

articles.summary: Explosive growth in imported vehicles omitted from EV tariffs fuels concern for future of European carmakers

blocks.text: Sales of Chinese hybrid cars have rocketed in the EU in the past four and a half years, new data shows, underlining growing concerns in Brussels over the future of the European car industry.

In 2022, just 659 Chinese-made fully hybrid cars (vehicles in which the petrol or diesel engine charge the motor and battery) were sold in the EU. However, after Brussels imposed anti-subsidy tariffs on fully electric cars from China in 2024, sales of hybrids have shot up to 160,662 in the first seven months of this year.

Eurostat figures show that sales of Chinese-made plug-in hybrid vehicles – models popular for longer driving distances which can recharge via both the fuel engine and an external power source – have also soared, rising from 56,706 sold in 2022 to 217,764 from January to July this year.

The volume of Chinese hybrids on the roads is now spooking the car industry and Brussels, which has asked China to voluntarily reduce its hybrid exports to the EU or face safeguards, likely to be quotas.

According to new figures released by the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA), hybrid cars now account for almost 37% of the overall market, with electric cars making up just over 21% of the market.
ACEA figures showed three Chinese manufacturers – BYD, Chery, and Leapmotor – making significant inroads with triple-digit growth in the EU.

A fourth firm, Geely, has had a steady 8% increase in the first eight months of the year, and remains the most popular Chinese brand in the EU with 205,000 cars sold in the first eight months of the year. Its brands include Sweden’s Volvo and Polestar, the EU’s only all-electric car manufacturer.
BYD is catching up with Geely with sales year-on-year rocketing 163% with 177,000 units sold.
Both firms, along with a fifth Chinese manufacturer, SAIC, are now firmly ahead of Elon Musk’s Tesla which sold 142,000 cars across the bloc in the first seven months of the year.
European car manufacturers still dominate with the Volkswagen group selling 2m cars in the first eight months of the year.

Sales of electric cars are also growing fast in parts of Europe including Germany, up 75% to 69,000 units in August, and in France, where sales are up by 112%. In Slovenia sales have increased by 266%. This compares with the UK, up 27% in August to 28,000 EVs sold and Ireland up just 7% to 2,200 units.

Earlier this month, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, described the now €1.18bn-a-day trade deficit between the bloc and China as having reached an unsustainable “tipping point”.
after newsletter promotion
The EU’s trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his Chinese counterpart Wang Wentao will meet on 8 and 9 October to try to build a truce.
Also hoping for a trade truce are Donald Trump and Xi Jinping who meet in their third summit in 12 months in Washington on Thursday.

Trump agreed in South Korea last October to drop tariffs on certain Chinese imports in exchange for a suspension of China’s export restriction on rare earths, critical to the car industry across the US, EU and the UK.
Some believe a deal may not have been reached yet and the suspension may not be announced until the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation conference next month.

articles.title: Panelo: Excluding absent senators from impeachment vote violates Constitution
articles.summary: The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte said Thursday the Senate impeachment court violated the Constitution when it voted to base the two-thirds vote to convict on the number of senators who are…

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 4:33pm

The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte said Thursday that the Senate impeachment court violated the Constitution when it voted to base the two-thirds vote to convict on the number of senators who are capable of "legally and factually participating in the impeachment proceedings."

“This is a clear violation of our Constitution because the Constitution states two-thirds of all members of the Senate are needed for conviction. They changed this yesterday,” Atty. Paolo Panelo said during an Unang Balita interview.
He further said it is not within the power of the Senate to make the change "so this is grave abuse of discretion."
“While the impeachment court is sui generis (a class of its own), it should still follow due process and the Constitution. It was clear to us the ruling did not follow the Constitution,” he added.
Panelo, however, could not say for sure if the Vice President’s camp will raise the issue before the Supreme Court.
Article 11, Section 6 of the Constitution states that “the Senate shall have the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment.”

The same provision also states that “No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate”, although it does not state a specific number for what constitutes two-thirds.
In a separate press conference, House prosecutor Terry Ridon of Bicol Saro party-list said the defense or those who disagree with the new threshold are free to go to the Supreme Court.
“If they think they have a case, they are free to go to the Supreme Court. We will wait for that petition and whatever the Supreme Court decides, we will abide by that,” he said.
Ridon, however, also said critics are free to lick their wounds over the decision of the Senate impeachment court on the threshold.
“Sa mga nagsasabi po na this is manipulated at kung ano ano pa ‘yung mga sinasabi nila, may tissue rito, punasan ninyo ang luha ninyo,” Ridon added.

The Senate impeachment court on Wednesday voted to base the two-thirds vote to convict Duterte on the number of senators who are capable of "legally and factually participating in the impeachment proceedings."
Excluded members are those:

items: detained and/or suspended or otherwise legally restrained from exercising the functions of a senator,
persons sought by authorities and whose whereabouts are unknown,
suffering from a physical or medical incapacity,
beyond the coercive processes of the Senate, and
others similarly situated.

articles.title: Why India's Election Commission is in the eye of a storm - again
articles.summary: India's polling monitor is facing yet another crisis of credibility with fresh allegations against its chief.

blocks.text: India's Election Commission (ECI) is facing yet another crisis of credibility after a series of fresh allegations of irregularities against its chief.

One of the most trusted public institutions in the world's largest democracy, the three-member commission is headed by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and includes Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as commissioners.

The latest row broke out after a report in the Indian Express newspaper, external said that in the past few months, CEC Kumar had been repeatedly questioned by his two colleagues over the integrity of the voter database, changes to the way new voters are enrolled and the security of the electoral rolls itself.

The report said that Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi objected to several decisions which were taken without their knowledge. There were at least 14 times in the past 10 months when Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi were kept in the dark, it added.
In one instance, the report says, the two commissioners even wrote a letter complaining to the chief secretary, the top bureaucrat in the Indian government.

The revelations have created a furore, with opposition leaders demanding Kumar's resignation. Sandhu and Joshi have not publicly commented on the report but the ECI said in a statement that "differing views" were part of the "decision-making process".
The report comes at a time when the commission is carrying out a controversial country-wide revision of the electoral database.
The Election Commission says the aim of this Special Intensive Revision - better known by its acronym SIR - is to ensure that no ineligible name remains on the rolls.

It says the last revision was done nearly a quarter of a century ago and the voters' list needs to be updated to account for those who have died, left the country or are registered in more than one place as they've moved to a new address.

But the exercise has been mired in controversy from the start with the opposition parties accusing CEC Kumar of manipulating voters' list to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.
But the latest revelations are being seen as much more serious as they are about questions being raised from within the Election Commission about the way its chief is functioning.
From the start, questions have lingered over the robustness of the revision, which has seen 130 million names from across India struck off the voters' list.

Millions of voters have also complained to the authorities that their names are missing, saying the new process set by SIR to register as voters is too cumbersome and involves furnishing documents that many don't have.
Former CEC SY Quraishi, who says he has "been a critic of the SIR from the beginning", told news agency PTI that he always wondered why Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had been "keeping quiet".
"[Now] I realised that very silently and quietly they were protesting, they were writing notes. That is a good thing, they have gone up in my esteem," he said.

items: How a Brazilian woman became the face of India vote fraud row
New voters list in Indian state includes wrong photos and dead people
The row over 'vote theft' that has shaken Indian politics

blocks.text: The revelations have also provided fresh ammunition to the opposition parties and critics who have repeatedly claimed that SIR is being used to exclude their voters for the BJP's benefit and that elections in India are no longer free and fair.

On Wednesday, angry opposition politicians once again questioned the sanctity of India's election process and demanded that CEC Kumar resign, saying he had no right to continue in office, with some even calling for his arrest.

The charge was led by MP and senior Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi who has repeatedly accused the Commission of "stealing votes from the opposition". On Wednesday, he also accused the Commission and its officers of "treason".

"Vote chori [theft] is a crime against the Indian people and a direct attack on our constitution. The BJP, RSS [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh] and EC who organised it have committed an act of treason. Justice will be served," he posted on X, external. He also shared a 15-second video telling the commission and its officers that "your time will come. You cannot get away".

Mamata Banerjee, leader of the regional Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, called for Kumar's arrest and demanded fresh polls with the pre-SIR voters' list in the state of West Bengal which she lost to the BJP in the recent elections. At least 2.7million voters were removed in the state during SIR - Banerjee and her supporters say that cost them dozens of seats and the election win.
Within hours of the Indian Express report and statements from opposition leaders, the Election Commission put out a statement, external defending its way of working.
"Differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution. They are a part of the decision-making process before a final decision is taken.
"Not only the three Commissioners, but every officer of the Commission is fully authorised to give his suggestions to the Commission for improving the electoral system," the statement said.

The note said that highlighting "certain specific internal notes and observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives" give only part of the picture.

And that in recent months, the commission has "introduced around 40 new initiatives and undertaken many electoral reforms including the conduct of electoral roll revision (including SIR) across the country. All these decisions are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission in the past one year".
The BJP has also defended CEC Kumar, calling the opposition criticism a "smear campaign" and that dissent was "a sign of a vibrant democracy".

Party spokesperson Sambit Patra told a press conference that "ever since the Modi government came to power in 2014, opposition parties have been collapsing one after the other". And because they cannot win elections, they are trying to "undermine the institutions of the country", he said.

items: Indian journalists condemn 'denial' of voting and passport rights of prominent editor
Why India's Election Commission is facing a test of credibility

blocks.text: But the row over the election database is likely to intensify. Banerjee has already said opposition parties will hold protests until Kumar remains CEC.
And India's influential Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which recently forced the education minister to resign, has also said it will protest against the "hijacking of India's democracy".

Analysts say the defence of the Election Commission is unlikely to satisfy many, with some pointing out that its statement doesn't address all the issues raised in the newspaper report and that "CEC Kumar needs to clear the air, external if we are to view the Commission as an impartial body".

articles.title: Benjamin Netanyahu to deliver defiant UN speech while facing protests and political isolation
articles.summary:
Prime minister will ‘highlight Israel’s achievements’ as he heads towards his toughest re-election challenge

When he takes the stage at the UN on Thursday, Benjamin Netanyahu will deliver a…
articles.byline: Andrew Roth and Alice Speri in New York

blocks.text: When he takes the stage at the UN on Thursday, Benjamin Netanyahu will deliver a familiar message of defiance even as protests and international condemnation leave the Israeli leader in growing isolation.

Netanyahu is facing his toughest re-election challenge in a political career spanning decades with three ongoing conflicts in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, and a growing campaign of violence by Israeli settlers in the West Bank.

Internationally, Israel is facing growing condemnation. The UK, France and Canada are planning to sanction Israeli settlements in the West Bank, and the British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has accused Israeli settlers of committing ethnic cleansing of Palestinian communities.

And the US is in the midst of a historic shift in public opinion against Israel, with 62% of respondents telling Pew in July they had a negative opinion of Netanyahu’s government, and 60% of American Jews in a poll released this week hoping he is voted out in October.

Protests are expected both in the UN’s general assembly hall and on the streets of New York City, where mayor Zohran Mamdani has tempered his earlier promises to arrest Netanyahu as a war criminal to assure demonstrators this week that he would protect their “right to [protest] in this city”.

Danny Danon, Israel’s ambassador to the UN, defended Netanyahu’s government in a telephone interview before this week’s speech seeking to cast criticism of Israel’s actions as the product of misinformation and bias.

“We are aware of the fact that we had a very challenging three years since October 7,” said Danon. “We accomplished a lot, but we were criticised. We were under the spotlight, and for us, I think, we are proud of our achievements.”
“At the same time, we will work harder to improve the image of Israel, and we know there’s a campaign against us,” he added.

Anger at Netanyahu will be on full display in New York City on Thursday, where several protests have been scheduled, including one from Bryant Park in midtown Manhattan to the UN headquarters in Turtle Bay to “reject war criminal Benjamin Netanyahu and the genocidal Zionist project”.
“Netanyahu is coming to New York amid a political environment that has made it crystal clear that he is not welcome here,” said Beth Miller, the political director of Jewish Voice for Peace Action.

She described a “mainstreaming” of public opinion that “Americans do not want to be supporting Israel’s genocide. We do not want to be supporting Israel’s apartheid. We do not want to be arming Israel or supporting Israel.”

And Palestinian representatives are calling for diplomatic missions to bring staff for a planned walkout of Netanyahu’s speech to “send a clear message to Netanyahu and his government that no one is willing to aid, abet, or be complicit in its genocide and war crimes and illegal occupation, which all peace-loving states and peoples demand must come to an end”.

But in Danon’s telling, Israel’s problem was largely one of public relations rather than of policy, and he cited a “wave of misinformation” as the reason for the precipitous shift in polling. Netanyahu would use his speech to “highlight Israel’s achievements”, he said, and to lay out “what still should be done, and how should we verify that we actually achieve the goals of the war?”

He did not elaborate on those specific measures before the speech, but the White House and US policymakers will be listening as they calibrate their message to voters – as well as the backlash of public anger – ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

Netanyahu is expected to deliver a hardline message aimed not just at world leaders, but also to his own electorate in Israel ahead of the October elections. “I think that he is trying to demonstrate to the Israeli populace that he still maintains some level of control over the situation,” said Miller. “And I think that he is trying to speak to a rightwing audience and a Trump-Maga audience in this country to try to rile up the hatred and Islamophobia.”

Donald Trump and top US officials are not expected to meet with Netanyahu, however, during a visit expected to last less than 24 hours. Trump will be in Washington DC to host the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, and Netanyahu has cited Israel’s electoral campaign and the holiday of Sukkot as his reason to head home quickly after the speech.
A Trump administration official said Netanyahu’s delegation had sought a high-level meeting during the visit but none was organised. There are also no plans to meet congressional leaders, Danon said.

With criticism from top Republicans, including the vice-president, JD Vance, and leading democratic presidential contenders, Israel could face a 2028 campaign with two candidates who no longer support arms sales to Israel or the broad diplomatic support that it has enjoyed in the past.
Even within the Maga base there are fractures, Miller noted, with “more and more people who don’t really want to be sending our tax dollars to support the Israeli government”.

Danon said of a potential shift in the US-Israeli security relationship: “I think that we are still sharing the same values, and that’s why I’m sure that we will continue to have the support from the US.”

But there are multiple flashpoints now for anger from both US political parties, as well as the international community, including dire humanitarian concerns and the lack of reconstruction in Gaza, the expansion of settlements in the West Bank, and continued conflicts in Lebanon and Iran, where the US has found itself mired in a conflict that has driven up global energy prices.

Asked if a controversial $2.8bn (£2.1bn) arms sale indicated that Israel is preparing to resume its offensive in Gaza, Danon said Israel “hopes that we will see [Hamas’s] disarmament without our involvement”, nodding to efforts by the Trump-backed Board of Peace. But he said Israel “will do it ourselves” if that does not change, adding: “We can not leave it forever like that.”

He was equally resolute on the West Bank, saying that Israel would not be swayed by recent criticism led by the UK over plans to expand settlements including E1, the planned construction which would sever East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank.

Senate Democrats are also introducing a bill on Wednesday to sanction facilitators of the new settlement, and Senator Chris Coons, a co-sponsor, said in a statement that “as Palestinian civilians face a campaign of devastation and fear from violent extremist settlers, the United States must send a strong message that this behaviour is unacceptable”.
The protests began even before Netanyahu arrived in New York.

Already on Wednesday, several members of the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter rallied at the city’s John F Kennedy international airport in protest at weapons and explosive materials destined for the Israeli military being flown out of the airport on commercial aircraft.

Aber Kawas, who in November is slated to become the first Palestinian-American elected official in New York state, spoke at the event and later told the Guardian she plans to join many other New Yorkers protesting Nethanyahu’s UN speech on Thursday.
“Thousands of people are against his presence in our city,” she said.

Even though some had hailed Netanyahu’s decision to cut his visit short as a victory, she added, “the fact that he is coming shows he continues to have a sense of entitlement to be centred on the world stage while being the head architect of a genocide”.

articles.title: Labour likely to be biggest party in hung parliament, mega poll suggests – UK politics live
articles.summary:
The poll shows Reform UK ‘neck-and-neck’ with the Conservative party

Good morning. Andy Burnham and Kemi Badenoch are both preparing for their party conferences (next week, and the following…

blocks.text: Good morning. Andy Burnham and Kemi Badenoch are both preparing for their party conferences (next week, and the following week, respectively), and this morning YouGov has released a new MRP poll with encouraging news for both of them. Polling is very good at revealing electoral trends, but a lot less good at predicting electoral outcomes, and wise politicians don’t treat them as gospel. But they also find polling impossible to ignore, not least because it shapes the landscape within which parties operate. A leader expecting to win the next election acts differently from one expecting to lose it.
And would Burnham win an election held now? Not exactly, according to the YouGov figures, but Labour would be the largest party. Here is YouGov’s summary of its results.

double quotation mark-Labour would be the largest party in a hung parliament, were an election held tomorrow, winning 241 seats in our model’s central estimates -Such a result would be a net loss of 170 seats for Labour on the 2024 election, but is up from our MRP this time last year, which projected the party would be reduced to just 144 seats and showed Reform UK within touching distance of a majority -Reform UK are now neck-and-neck with the Conservatives, with the parties respectively on 123 and 130 seats in our median projection -Our central projection shows the Lib Dems on 71 seats, the SNP on 40, Plaid Cymru on 15, and the Greens on nine -37% of constituencies are decided by margins of five points or less in our central estimate, with this rising to 67% of seats projected to be won by Reform UK

blocks.caption: YouGov MRP poll results Photograph: YouGov

blocks.text: This is not a terrific result for Labour, but the party is in a much better position under Burnham than it was under Keir Starmer.

The YouGov figures suggest Badenoch has no chance of forming a government. But she may be even happier with these numbers than Burnham. A year ago polling suggested Nigel Farage was on course to be the next prime minister, and there was serious talk about the Conservative party being totally eclipsed by Reform UK. Not anymore. Today’s figures have the Tories narrowly ahead of Reform on the central estimate (the best guess – YouGov also has highest and lowest estimates for seat numbers). More importantly, the poll confirms that Farage’s hopes of forming a government are – for now at least – fading.

blocks.caption: YouGov MRP poll results Photograph: YouGov
YouGov MRP poll results Photograph: YouGov

blocks.text: YouGov surveyed almost 17,000 people for the poll, between 23 August to 18 September.
I will post more on the poll as the day goes on. There will be other news too, although there is not a lot in the diary.

articles.title: DOJ seeks more confidential funds in 2027 budget, cites 'more challenges'
articles.summary: The Department of Justice (DOJ) and its attached agencies are seeking higher confidential funds for their operations in 2027, it was disclosed during the Senate budget hearing on Thursday.

blocks.text: Published September 24, 2026 3:43pm
The Department of Justice (DOJ) and its attached agencies are seeking higher confidential funds for their operations in 2027, it was disclosed during the Senate budget hearing on Thursday.
The DOJ has a P579.4 million budget for confidential funds, which is 47.3% lower than 2026's P1.1 billion budget.
Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida has sought the restoration of P500 million to the Office of the Secretary, noting that only P319.9 million was allocated under the NEP.
“Sa Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking, napapansin po namin sa inter-agency na ang P10 million ay kulang at talaga kailangan pa naming dagdagan dahil may dagdag pong hamon,” Vida said.
(For the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking, we have observed that the P10 million allocation is insufficient, and we really need to increase it because we are facing additional challenges.)

He also hoped that Congress would grant DOJ’s budget of P475,000 to combat emerging cybercrime and P5 million for the National Coordination Center Against Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children and Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM).
Bureau of Immigration (BI) Commissioner Joel Viado also sought an additional P10 million to P20 million for his agency’s 2027 confidential funds.
He said the additional budget would help the agency in hiring more personnel.
“Nagre-request kami sa DBM ng additional positions. Ang aming fugitive search unit, ang humahabol o tumutugis sa mga pugante, wala pang 20 ’yan (nationwide),” Viado said.
(We are requesting additional positions from the Department of Budget and Management. Our Fugitive Search Unit, which tracks down and apprehends fugitives, has fewer than 20 personnel.)
Meanwhile, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is seeking a P1 billion budget for its confidential funds since the agency is planning to procure equipment to combat cybercrime.

“We are requesting sana about P1 billion divided into 12 months. Because more than the expenses on operations namin, we are intending to procure tools and equipment to fight cybercrime,” NBI Director Melvin Matibag said.

He shared that during its meetings with the United States Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) and Thailand’s Central Investigation Bureau (CIB), the NBI found that many scams are linked to the Philippines.
“Nire-request naming increase sana dito for the confidential funds is for us to procure these tools to fight ang ganito mga criminal activities,” Matibag said.
(We are requesting an increase in the confidential funds so we can procure the necessary tools to combat these types of criminal activities.)
He added that since April, the NBI has been conducting around 200 to 220 investigative operations.
The BI and NBI are attached agencies under the Justice Dept.
For 2027, the DOJ proposed a budget of P46.435 billion, which is equivalent to 0.64% of the P7.2-trillion national budget.

Of DOJ’s total proposed budget, P31.723 billion (68.32%) was allotted for Personnel Services (PS), P11.340 billion (24.42%) for Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE), and P3.372 billion (7.26%) for Capital Outlay (CO). —RF, GMA News
